3.5 5 Stars Check out my review http thebookbanner.blogspot.com 201...

3.80 Okay. so. this book had wonderful concepts. voodoo, New Orleans, 150 year old curses, a ghost and human love affair. but details were lacking, and I felt like the author tried to jam everything in. it would have been much more enjoyable if there were details on Alex and Lucy, the setting, etc. I still enjoyed the book, but it was a bit dissapointing. especially because it had so much potential and had all the things I loved. and the ending was quite depressing. now she needs to write a book where Alex and Lucy find each other again. I know happy endings aren't always realistic, but it would've been nice!

3.5 stars The majority of the book was purely a cute story of an adorable couple - a red head girl, and a half Korean boy. And they are in fact really cute Eleanor is sometimes annoying, Park on the other hand is an angel . It's easy to breeze through the book and finish it in a day or two. The main twist of the story happens at the very end... and while it was a good ending, it almost surprises you that the story finished. I kept thinking "wait did I somehow skip reading something important, or am I missing a page?" Why 3 stars though? Not enough things events happen in the book. I don't like when a book is "all right" until about the last 10 of it. This book was sadly that way. If you're looking for a bubbly and sickeningly sweet story though, definitely pick this one up!

Once again, I kind of hate that I am so addicted to this book. This one was a bit more frustrating than the last one, but I still enjoyed it. I still was interested in what was happening, I still shipped my shipps, and gasped at all of the right placed. Kiera Cass is very good at writing books that I can read without thinking. Like at all.

I wouldn't say that I enjoyed this novel it was more that I appreciated it. It is all jagged edges, the brusque tone like sandpaper to the skin - and that's why it was so strong. It is the impeccably woven story of Sephora, a girl coming into her own identity as an artist and a woman. Her relationships are fascinating and grotesque a parasitic yet loving connection with her beautiful mother, her prickly yet loyal attachment to her best friend, and her own self-loathing yet self-preserving nature. But what I truly appreciated about this story was the way that Elana Arnold retold fairytales and Greek myths to build up the plot. The book was steeped in sexuality, but it wasn't sensual. Rather it takes you by a fistful of your hair and drags you into the painful, embarrassing and awkward journey to self-discovery. I wasn't surprised by Sephora's secret, but I don't think that was the point. I was swept up in the narrative, amused by her snark and heartbroken by her pain. In the end, it's not about "enjoying" it's about understanding, and that's why I liked it so much. This was a great read with a killer title. More reviews atA Story Addict

I loved the second book and I can't help but wonder if there will be a third.... and I checked and there will be a third, how exciting. It just left you at, "thats it, really?" It was really good and I loved it, and yes you must read the first because you might be totally lost. This book is totally about Kate and Vincent overcoming their odds as not being just any regular couple. You do find out that Vincent is considered, prophisized as the champion to Revenant Legend, and that equals danger for Kate and Vincent. Kate has found a story called Immortal Love where it foretells of a couple, a man who is young and a woman who is old that is in search of a gradesseur who is like a healer who could help the couple. But at the end of the story it came out that before they could get to the healer the woman dies. Kate finds two books, because in each, a part is missing, where they could find that ancient healer. She does find the healer but little does she know that when she does that, danger is soon to follow. The revenants are betrayed by one of their own and its by an unlikely suspect. But if you were to look back it totally make sense, and the person who betrays the revenants is the new leader of the Numa. I don't want to give away what happens so you have to read this for yourself, you will be so happy that you did. But be warned the end is sad and just know that thats not the end that there will be a third. Hope you like it as much as I did. I can't wait for the third book to come out. A must read!
I didn't like the love triangle or Belly really, but for whatever reason, this trilogy hooked me in. I couldn't stop reading these books until I knew who Belly was going to end up with.

I can't state enough how much I really liked this story. What started out as a girl hell bent on revenge turns into a story of finding a new life. Sarah does a beautiful job with this book. There wasn't any point of this story that I thought was slow. Once more, a beautifully done piece.
Nick acted like a grade school student with his teasing.. He's sweet though..so that makes up for it.

A stunning fantasy with original ideas and a build-up of action with a truly great reward. This is the type of story you could definitely call an epic journey - secret missions, hidden identities and some delicious high drama. Bonus I'm pretty sure this is a standalone book! I wanted to re-read this book as soon as I finished it. Do NOT miss this one!

There is a lot more character development here. Jared's and Kami's pain and adjustment without the link, the villians coming out to play, Ash's "bunnykiller" character, with wonderful secondary cast of Anegla, Holly, Kami's father and Lillian is good. Gave us a better and deeper insight of the complexities of relationship. Even more dialogues with Rusty was fun. Note but pls don't spoil his character with YET ANOTHER romance angle. However, the romance angle was a little overwrought. In addition, Jared is sometimes so angtsy I feel like slapping him, and Kami is so dense I wonder if journalism is really for her. The plot also did not progress that much until near the ending. And the ending Jared, really??!! the foolhardly heroics again?!! And the moping over Ash??!! Pls, Ash is a useless bunnykiller with no mind and backbone of his own!!! In addition, being caught by Rob Lynburn and to be broken sounds a little too much like the ending of "Catching Fire" of the Hunger Games. I feel a simlar reprisal of "Peeta hating Katniss" to "Jared hating Kami" coming along....

Although this is a dramatic story, the author demonstrates her sense of humor. I particularly enjoyed the opening scene when the main character, Rebecca, answers someone asking about the things a Catholic worships. The list and Rebecca's reactions are hilarious. The author also portrays a sensitive, intelligent, and brave Rebecca in this second book of the series as she faces her antagonist. Rebecca's concern and caring for other individuals and her prayers for them touched my heart. Although I purchased the first book of the series, I received a copy of this book from the author in exchange for my honest review.

This is the third time in a month the second book I have read in a series has been significantly better than the first one. I liked CATCHING JORDAN a lot, other than the ridiculous idea that an over-protective father would allow a teenage boy to sleep regularly in his teenage daughter's bed because they were, "Just Friends" Let me tell you, as a father of daughters, not even a particularly over-protective one, this just is not going to happen!. This book, however had better characters, not a ridiculous plot point like that, and was more heart-felt and compelling all around. It got a little preachy from time to time, but the family church was an important plot point and despite the fact people droning on and about about god gives me a rash, it worked in the story. Well worth the read and looking forward to the third in the series.

Fantastic book. Stayed up till almost 5 in the morning to finish it. The prose is like a drink of ice-cold water. The next time somebody tells me all YA is vapid or shallow or poorly written, I can point them to TEACH ME.

Better than the first. I'm still angry she is linked to Ash. And Jared!!!!!!!! Oh how much I love him and what he did to save Lillian and Ten. And I felt bad for him when his mother died. And i can't believe it ended like that, they need to save him no ASAP.

Uhm, well,... I was enjoying it at first it is a kid's spy novel, one of the kids knows tae kwon do and the other is a good magician, the dialogue is fun, just kind of offbeat enough. But pretty soon the story starts tripping over itself. Angela takes out 2 Mossad agents with her nifty tae kwon do and Q foils an agent with a card trick. Agents are going this way and that, shedding wigs, changing accents, planting bugs, putting more agents in place, playing obscure footage of an angel or is it a leopard? Who got killed, who didn't? Why? The implausability just kept increasing, characters kept changing looks, alliances, stories. Just spin me in a circle with a blind fold on, then explain to me how the Mossad and terrorists are all confused and I am supposed to figure it out. That was what the reading experience was a like, on a 6th grade level. And the Mossad doesn't need me to defend them, but I found the portrayal of them in this book to be verging on offensive.

I received this book from the publisher for free via NetGalley in return for an honest review. This is easily one of the worst books I've ever read and I honestly wonder if I'm reading the same book as everyone else who seems to love it. This is the second book in the series and if you do wish to read this series for yourself, then you must read Red Queen before this one. This book picks up literally where Red Queen leaves off and covers more political intrigue for the world and lots of endless boring action. Who knew action could be so boring? I must admit, I wasn't a massive fan of Red Queen, but I decided to read this one because I wanted to give Aveyard a second chance. It is evident that her writing is clearly not for me. I just find the writing too flat, there is nothing to make me care about the characters at all. The characters also don't feel real, they are far too two dimensional. The plot lacks any sort of interest and the writing itself just doesn't pull me in. I found this a genuine slog to get through. The endings of each book are always a little better, as if she is trying to make you think that the book was amazing after all so that you buy the next in the series. I honestly don't plan to continue on with this series currently, as I just have no desire to be bored for several hours. This all said, if you really enjoyed Red Queen, you will probably enjoy this one as I thought Red Queen was only average at best.

It's May--time for Kim's readathon! Can she catch up to her 200 book pace? It's looking good with my first library haul. Two back catalog Beth Kephardt's--always worthy. Rosie's summer is centered around her dying grandfather, and she takes the slow time to figure out lots about life and how it is best lived. Kephardt has a slow, steady touch with characters and events, and I savor every word.

I think my comments during my reading progress kind of say it all. One day I might try to finish this - it's so short, it seems doable... but then it's just SO BAD AS WELL. ETA 24 04 12 - Guess what? This was my seventh and final book for the 24-hour read-a-thon on Sunday! I decided to give it one last go. And okay I didn't actually finish it on Sunday, but I managed to get over halfway through. It took me about two hours to read all of fifty pages. I was getting really distracted by Bones on TV, and then book is just SO not engaging at ALL. But I did it. I picked it up again yesterday morning, and I managed to finish it. I was going to say it actually got a little better as it went on, but I think it's better to say that it got marginally less bad. I really can't give it more than one star because I honestly did not like any of it. I didn't like any of the characters there was not one which I was even remotely interested in! And there were a lot of characters. I just didn't like them. The book reads like a really bad episode of Heartbreak High. Now I loved Heartbreak High at the time, when I was younger than them and they were all SO grown-up and dangerous and different from anyone I knew. But now I'm older than them, I just look back and think - well they're all totally unrealistic when I think of my own life. I have never known anybody like that at all. I just can't believe in them being real. And maybe they are - but not to me. See, these kids are the ones who make fun of Toorak toffs, and play "spot the private school kid". I was that private school kid. And yeah, reading this book just turned me into an even bigger snob. I couldn't get invested in these kids because they just repulsed me... okay maybe that's a bit strong? But they were just SO over the top and unappealing. Yes, I looked down my nose at them all. I admit it! There was also way too much dialogue, and not enough action. It was hard to get to know any of the characters at all because you only ever heard them speak, and saw the very cardboard pictures of them, you never got to really KNOW them. Not that I think I'd have liked any of them anyway. Just not my types. It's also incredibly dated, in the kind of hilarious way now... like when someone's dad talks about how if there are two TV shows on at the same time then you have to absolutely choose ONE, unless you want to hire a video recorder. Brilliant. Also, this book has the ugliest cover I have ever seen, omg. Manuela, you'll love this one P

When reading this, I actually regretted having read Twilight. I enjoyed Twilight, even while recognizing its flaws. Unfortunately, my time reading Beautiful Creatures was spent thinking how much better it was than Twilight. I do think that BC was better written, and I'm sorry that I was distracted from its world by these thoughts. For me, the biggest strength of Beautiful Creatures were the two main characters. They were both honestly teenage without being obnoxious, or at least only occasionally annoying - . Both Ethan and Lena had enough depth to be interesting. The secondary characters were good, if mostly a little shallowly written. They covered enough variety to make up for that! I also was intrigued by the magical world, with a mythology not directly related to any other I've encountered. Working withing an existing mythology isn't a problem for me, but I liked the creativity of this one, particularly since it seemed well thought through. The other thing that stood out to me while reading was how some of the common conventions of YA paranormal romances were turned on their heads-- the primary example being the normal male teen and the powerful supernatural female teen! This wasn't a deep read, but it was a fun one!
This was a fun book to read. Loved all the characters and loved the ending!

Wow. Wow. Wow. Seriously, Maggie Stiefvater blew my mind with this book. I mean, I was expecting something good since the book sounded really interesting, but I was a little scared since I wasn't the biggest fan of Shiver and the rest of that series. Yet, I this book was I simply couldn't put down, and was so sad to finally part with once I was done. I absolutely adored the world Maggie created, the characters she gives us. There's something simply addicting to this novel. I can't really decide who I liked more, Blue or the Raven boys. On one side, there's something really unique about Blue, something strange and intriguing. On the other side, there's something really captivating about the four boys, all so different, yet sharing a deep bound. Adam, Ronan, Gansey and Noah all made ma like them for different reasons, and I find it hard to choose who was the most interesting one though I do have a small preference for Gansey, even if I needed to get to know him before really liking him. Maggie Stiefvater really created a novel full of twits and amazingly well crafted. There's something really beautiful about the novel, making me unable to stop reading. I can't seem to find a negative thing to say about this book, since I've fallen in love so hard with this novel. Only the good stood out to me, because the story is THAT addicting. I really can't wait to find out what will happen next to Blue and company. I still have some questions left unanswered, which I hope will find their answer in the next books. Seriously, even if you didn't enjoy the Wolves of Mercy Fall series, you should read it. To me, they were worlds apart. This book was simply amazing, and I hardly can wait for the next book. Definitely worth reading!

Still wants to be with him even thou he admits to killing people. and she gets drugged at a party, still not concerned. hit on her family, still no concerned. the only think that concerns her is that the "cute" boy takes notice of her and doesn't care that her family and his tells her to stay away. spoiler alert I started reading this because of the movie advert. I saw the advert, thought WOW and looked forward to seeing it. Then I discovered it was a book. I thought - even better - a book I can read right away, a book that is a series and I can always catch the movie afterwards and compare the two. What I loved about this book, the first in the Caster Chronicles, is that it's from Ethan's perspective. The whole book is through Ethan's POV. I wasn't expecting that, after seeing the advert for the film and reading what the book is about. It really works. This is the second book I've read recently, that is essentially a teen romance mixed with the supernatural, which is told from the lead male's POV. I think this really works. There's more mystery, more intrigue and it's less...for lack of a better word...soppy. In this book, you have no idea what's going on with Lena or with Ethan himself, because Ethan doesn't know. A large part of the story plot is a locket that gives Lena and Ethan visions of the Civil War era, and glimpses of the lives of Genevieve Duchannes and Ethan Carter Wate, Ethan and Lena's great-great-great- relations. I loved this part. Each time they stepped into this story, I was even more enthralled, even more caught up in the mystery and drama and romance. I think the mirror of Ethan and Lena's relationship with Genevieve and Ethan's is subtle, intriguing and adds to the overall mystery of what is going on between both couples. I really liked Uncle Macon, and Link was a favourite too. I think the added part of Marian and her role between the Casters and the Mortals was inspirational, it's always great to have an impartial character hanging around for those sticky moments. It was a total shame to lose someone from the story, but sometimes the story just calls for it. It worked and it was gut-wrenching when you realised what had happened. I really loved the twists, the never knowing and the dynamic relationships. Overall, reading Beautiful Creatures is like being sucked into Lena's notebook with no choice, no backing out and no option but to see it through to the end. There's no putting it down. You open the cover and you have to see it through to the other side.

I usually don't review books I didn't finish, and I tried so hard to finish this book, but I just had to stop. This is my second chance for Rainbow Rowell and I just don't think she is my kind of author. I read Fangirl first and what I disliked about it is the same thing I disliked about Elanor Park, I found the narrator annoying and whinny. I had so many flip flop emotions with this book. At first I hated it and then I starting like it because of Elanor's home life. If the book was about her home life and how this teenager managed her way through a difficult situation I would like this book a whole lot more. Cut out the romance and give me a gritty coming to age novel. Just when I would start to like the Romance of her and Park a second later I would hate it, mostly because of Elanor. I might even enjoyed this book is it was just Park. I didn't mind Park at all and enjoyed his narration. I liked that at a young age he understood his privilege and I had some nostalgia for him because he was this cool punk rock kid who was into The Smiths and Buzzcock. The kind of kid I would have been into in high school....okay I am still into at 27 year old. All that being said, I just wanted to shake Elanor the same way I wanted shake Cath in Fangirl and tell them, "Just be honest, stop complicating everything." The on going whinny of Elanor and her back and fourth with Park of "Why do you like me?" drove me freaking crazy. I felt like a lot of her whinny could easily be explained by just saying her home life hard, her home life was rough, her step dad is an asshole. I didn't even have that much the book left to read I will admit and I just couldn't finish it.

spoiler alert I've come to hate Adelina. There's not other way for me to feel, frankly. She's becoming the bitchiest of stupid bitches and I'm so over her it isn't even funny. Please can we have the next book told from someone who isn't a whiny brat with too much power?

This is a great collection of snippets that provide insights into the Maze Runner series. When the solar flares burned out huge portions of the Earth, WICKED scientists figured there were too many people and not enough resources and released the Flare Virus. Announcements and bulletins from the early release of and panic over the Flare showcase what a terrible idea this population control attempt was. They tried to play God, and it blew up in their faces. I really have no sympathy for such an organization and zero trust that they'd make the right moral decisions. Emails within the group detail the start of the Trials, the Maze, and even some of what Thomas did. The glimpses into the boys' lives were also great. Thomas' first memory of the Flare's taking his father and the effect that had on his mother. Frypan's hope and elation at regaining his memories. Minho's bravado, loyalty, and tenacity in the face of being asked to betray his friends. These all add a layer of interest to these characters. I hope Dashner writes more like this!

Originally posted here As expected, Gemina blew my mind. Good Lord. Where to begin? Gemina is predominantly set upon jump station Heimdall and we get to meet a whole new cast of characters. Firstly there is privileged princess, Hanna, who is the only daughter of the station captain Hanna's boyfriend, heartthrob Jackson, a charismatic young member of the Heimdall security division there is Nik, a tattooed bad boy who is part of a notorious crime family then there is Ella, a talented hacker and Nik's cousin. Every main character in this book felt so real and absolutely jumped from the page, it took no time at all for me to quickly become emotionally invested in all of their stories. The main question at the end of Illuminae is explored in Gemina, the question being - after all of the distress calls that the Hypatia transmitted to jump station Heimdall, why didn't the station respond? Deep down, I was a teeny bit disappointed that Kady and Ezra were absent for much of the book but I loved the new characters so much that I couldn't dwell on it. My absolute favourite thing about this series is the mixed media and it does not disappoint in Gemina. There is the beautiful addition of Hanna's journal which showcases Marie Lu's illustrations. I think being able to view graphically Hanna's thoughts about Heimdall and the people in her life really made her personality come to life for me. Not to mention the diagrams of jump station Heimdall really assisted me in accurately imagining what it looked like, cause I would have NEVER imagined it properly. Gemina messes with your mind, it's surprisingly twisty and EXTREMELY fast paced. I felt overwhelmed at times because the pace was so fast, I would blink and something else would happen, it was tense y'all. The last third of the book in particular was my favourite and the ending is just phenomenal. I have only a few teeny tiny grumbles. In my opinion nothing could be as terrifying as the Phobos virus in Illuminae and so the seldom appearing alien predators in Gemina paled in comparison. I also felt like there was too many surveillance footage analyses, which was my least favourite format to read. To be honest, I loved Illuminae just that little bit more but Gemina is still a highly enjoyable sequel and well worth the read.

Alright, right off the bat I am going to be honest about something. I had a hard time at the beginning of Fire in Frost. I honestly considered DNF'ing the book, but there was enough of something there that I decided to give it a fair chance. In the end, I am happy that I didn't give up on it. It wasn't perfect, but giving it a shot was absolutely worth it. Fire in Frost centers around Crystal Frost, our MC. Her and one of her best friend's, Emma, walk in to school one morning, and there is a fundraiser being held for the one year anniversary of the death of a classmate. Without warning, Crystal starts feeling really strange. She starts looking around, and that is when she sees the ghost of Olivia, the very one the fundraiser is being held for. After that, she has one of her worst days. Once home from school, a series of events leads her to her mothers shop, and there she starts to learn the truth about Olivia, and the truth about who she really is. With the help of her BFF's, Emma and Derrick, she learns to control and channel her psychic powers, to help a girl who is in an abusive relationship, and play a few fun rounds of hide-and seek. My main issue with the story was the writing itself. It seemed a bit juvenile, and it just didn't flow well. It started to even out around the middle, and became a much better read because of it. Once the book hit it's stride, the plot became a lot more involving, the characters more like-able, and the story caught and held my interest. I finally began rooting for each of the characters. Crystal was a good MC, and I really liked Emma and Derrick. They stuck by her, even when they might have thought and called her crazy. The secondary characters were good additions to the story. The ending was good, with a good resolution, and the promise of more adventures to come. All in all, Fire in Frost was a good story. The ideas were sound, and intriguing. I think there is serious potential for a great second book in the series, because with the ending I have to think there will be one coming!
This book was so well done. The side-by-side stories of the two Fionas kept me turning the pages and gave me a lot to think about about the choices we make and the accidents that happen.

2 Stars DESCRIPTION Mother Nature is pissed. Few will survive. Jackie is loving her last year of summer camp, despite new-guy Xander, jerk extraordinaire. That is, until disaster strikes on the senior backpacking trip. At first, it seems like a nightmare, but Jackie quickly realizes that the huge fire and resulting carnage around her are as real as real gets. Miraculously and infuriatingly, in Jackie's opinion , Xander survives the burning, too, but that's the least of her worries. Mother Nature has wiped out millions and burned cities to the ground, plants are growing at a crazy-rapid rate, and fairytale creatures are very real--and very dangerous. Jackie and Xander must learn to survive sans food, shelter, and soap, and battle their way across the wild American landscape in search of their families--all without killing each other. Along the way, the duo learns that maybe the other isn't so terrible after all, but going months with no toothpaste isn't exactly a recipe for romance. Will the journey be too much for their growing relationship? Will it even be worth it at all? Or will their homes and families be burned to a crisp? REVIEW Jackie has been looking forward to her last year at summer camp, but things quickly fall apart when a new kid arrives...Xander. Sparks fly between the two, but not in a good way. Disaster strikes on their first night out on a week-long backpacking trip when mother nature decides to take the world back. Jackie and Xander soon discover that they're one of the few people to survive. Desperate to get back to their families, both decide to travel together across country, where they encounter mythical creatures and odd fairytale settings taken straight from wonderland. The two main characters have a huge case of hate at first sight. After the world ends, they spend months alone and I didn't feel any romantic connection between them, both coming off as bratty teenagers that just kind of end up with each other. So disappointing. Despite facing life and death choices, both kids are very one dimensional. A number of plot issues kept tripping me up. For example, Jackie learns how to survive out in the wilderness after one day. The book began interestingly enough, but the preachy attitude of how we're destroying the earth really got to me after a while. But what really put me over the top is one of the main characters, who saves their lives repeatedly, dies and they laugh it off. Not for me. It sounds like I hate the book, but I did enjoy some parts. The fantasy aspect, while not very believable, was unique and entertaining if a little too convenient at times. Overall, this book just wasn't for me. I was expecting a gritty dystopian novel and found myself disappointed. Posted from my site www.StaceyBrutger.com
Two stars. The second book in this trilogy was not nearly as good as the first. The writing seemed to be too simple. I'll still probably read the final book in the trilogy but not right now.

No matter how ready you think you are, you are never quite ready for this book. I didn't really know what this book was about when I realized I wanted it - I just thought it was cool that the main characters were named Aristotle and Dante, and I'd read the synopsis which also does not prepare you for this book , so I figured, hey, looks good, might as well check it out. For some reason I was tearing up a little in the first hundred pages, nearly crying off and on in the next two hundred, and totally sobbing at the end. It does have a happy ending, I wasn't crying because it was terribly sad. I don't even know why I was crying, it was just... this book was just so full of emotion. Now, the characters. The main character is Aristotle, who everyone calls Ari. He doesn't really like to talk much, and he thinks about his brother, who is in prison, a lot. One day he goes to the pool although he can't swim and meets Dante. Dante teaches him how to swim and thus a beautiful friendship is born. Dante is... well, it's sort of hard to explain Dante. Dante is Dante. He hates shoes, he talks too much, and he doesn't seem to have much of a filter. I loved both Aristotle and Dante, though I think Aristotle would have to be my favorite. The ending of the book was perfect. It was... I was crying but it was a beautiful way to end the book. That last sentence... The only thing I really had a problem with was with some of the dialogue, there were little to no dialogue tags and it was a little bit difficult to remember who was speaking when, but it was a minor thing and overall it didn't detract from the quality of the book. But, overall, I think that this book was amazing and I'll probably reread it many times.

This was a very disappointing read. I picked it up thinking that it would be a highly suspenseful, entertaining read. It was, at parts, but the overall story was a sad comparison to what it could have been. The beginning of the book didn't catch my interest, in fact, I almost gave up on the book after the first couple of chapters moved along at a snail's pace. Then, when the "twist" which was inevitable and all too predictable happened, I decided to give it a chance. Bad choice. Even though I was intrigued by some of the plot lines in the middle of the story, the majority never saw closure in the end. Thinking back, there was only ONE plot line that did see closure. It was by no means the most important nor the most exciting detail of the story, so I was confused when the book abruptly ended after that one minor detail was satisfied. The means by which the heroine and she really does not deserve that title received what she most wanted was ridiculous. I literally wanted to shoot her for being so stupid. Seriously, she would be the end of any life left on that post-apocalyptic world. In conclusion, the beginning of this book will bore, the middle will mildly entertain, and the end will surely not satisfy.

spoiler alert I know I should have stopped reading this when at the beginning chapter one of the characters said "FOSHO" but nosy me, I just had to see why this got glowing reviews. ok so let me start by saying this book reminds me so much of Twilight, which I wasn't particularly fond of. I didn't read any reviews prior to this, so I'm not copying anyone by saying that. I just found myself thinking, "Wow this is kind of like Twilight." The setting is an island which means everyone will know each other. A normal girl named Helen lives her life trying to survive school and basically an average teenage life. A rich family comes in and they are inhumanly beautiful and automatically popular. They drive fancy cars, they watch over her by sleeping on her rooftop, and the beautiful boy is controlling and possessive of her. He constantly touches and holds her hand, but refuses to speak up when she asks what exactly is going on. Instead of mind-reading like Edward Cullen, he can tell when people lie. He also has a sister that can see the future! Alice anyone? She also cooks, lives with her dad who never knows what's going on , and has a face of pure beauty but is completely oblivious to it. She's utterly, painfully shy and she likes to blend in the background. I have nothing against these people, since I for one am a very quiet and private person. I'm only stating how this quality reminds me of Bella. To be fair, she didn't fall instantly in love with Lucas. She actually tried to kill him in front of everyone but then a few chapters later when the need to kill is gone- instead of getting to know each other, they start holding hands and sleeping in beds together. I know she was meant to be a strong character, but I thought she was the complete opposite. I understand that she's supposed to be insecure and humble but she came off as weak and whiny. It doesn't make sense because she's so damn strong, but that's what made her so weak in my eyes. She had all these powers, and yet she could never think clearly. It was frustrating. Don't get me wrong, I love kick-ass female characters but in this one it was like every chapter there was something newly special about her. She's physically strong and fast she's impervious to knives, arrows, and swords plus, she can fly! Oh and she also shoots lightning bolts apparently. Yes she was a demi-god but come on, that was a little too much. I don't know, it felt like a fan-fiction to me or something. I didn't find the romance touching. The love interest Lucas, he never really explained why he was in love with her. It was sort of like, "I love you, only you. You're mine and let's run away together." There was no emotional connection. They were just two beautiful people that found each other I guess. I love Greek mythology. It's something that i used to obsess about since I was a small girl. I loved reading anything about it, and believe me I've read a ton but for some reason I couldn't stand this! Maybe I like to see my tragic heroes in an ancient era, uttering romantic words so unlike "Dickhead", "bullshit", "bro", and "jackass". The dialogue wasn't good. It was a little too... amateur? I don't mean to hurt anyone's feelings, i know people have different tastes so if you like this book then by all means enjoy it. I only wish to write down what i'm thinking at this moment. If you like romance, ever-lasting love, tragedy, and a female protagonist who can actually kick ass then you probably would enjoy this book. As for myself, I won't be reading the sequel.

I initially picked up the book, as I have a friend called Lynn Joseph, and while I knew it wasn't her, her name was the reason I plucked it off the shelf. Joseph is both a published poet and an attorney in the state of New York who says lawyers have no soul? . Each chapter starts with a poem. The story itself is simple, wistful, sad, and flows like a stream over pebbles. It never reaches any heights, or turns into a torrent, but it's a pleasant book all the same.

I am so sad because I am just....so disappointed. The premise of this book sounded so good. And the cover was interesting to me, kind of made me wonder why her hair was DNA? and I do appreciate what the author was going for. Nature vs Nurture But this book just made no sense. I didn't have a good basis as to why the government would just up and start testing AND THEN taking those kids, including our special snowflake Davy, out of their supportive and happy homes because....they have a strand in their DNA that with no science they have told me to back up their claim means these kids will be killers. Wait, what? Not only do they rip them out of their homes, but they shove them all next to each other - enclose them in a chain-link fence with a "teacher" guard on the outside and then...give them homework to work on? These kids are terrorized by the rougher of the group, completely at the mercy of the tougher students the bullies and the adults that all seem to want to.....grope the girls I'm so tired of this in YA books . and it just goes downhill from there....shipped off to other places, more extreme measures taken with all these "Killer" kids. spoiler alert A very refreshing YA fantasy novel with different premise that doesn't involve vampires or werewolves. The characters are likable and the plot is fast-pacing. I kinda wish though that the author had invested more on the worldbuilding, perhaps by describing the Windwalker world and their inhabitants more than simply focusing on getting the story going. There're some plot questions, such as why Audra's father couldn't learn the truth sooner despite the bonding thing that supposedly allow him to understand his wife more than other people. Some things are a bit too simplified like Vane's mother's easy acceptance of his true identity, the fighting never more than 2 Stormers to face at a time, and they're not very difficult to beat either , the Vane-Audra relationship the generic insta-love . Je ne sais pas pourquoi, mais j'attendais beaucoup de ce dernier tome. Je voulais qu'il contrebalance le tome 5 deja une deception pour terminer la serie en beaute. Il n'en est rien. Dans ce dernier tome Mead introduit de nouveaux personnages Joshua et Cie qui n'apportent finalement pas grand chose a l'intrigue et qui sont en plus peu developpes dans quel but? Remplir quelques pages probablement. A contrario, j'aurais aime en apprendre plus sur le lien entre Sydney et Abe. J'aurais aime qu'Eddie ne soit pas autant laisse de cote histoire de rattraper le tome precedent il sert un peu de bouche trou - Mead s'en sert quand elle en a besoin et l'oublie le reste du temps. Et Mia? Laissee a l'abandon egalement... Et puis le comportement de Rose est meprisable, j'en arrive a me demander comment j'ai pu croire en elle si longtemps. Elle se sert de ses "amis" mais elle n'est pas la pour eux, juste pour Lissa. Et encore, elle s'est servie de Lissa pour ramener Dimitri... Peut-on vraiment justifier l'aide inconditionnelle apportee par Mikhail, Eddie, Sydney, Mia, etc, au titre d'une amitie qui n'est finalement qu'unilaterale? Une bonne poire je veux bien, autant, j'ai du mal a y croire. Quant au triangle Dimitri-Rose-Adrian, quelle deception egalement. Tout ce melodrame pour ca? C'est niais. J'attendais plus de passion. D'autre part, je suis loin d'etre bilingue, mais il y a un certain nombres de fautes dans le livre. Mead a bacle son dernier tome, c'est mon impression.

Chasing Brooklyn is an extremely emotional book written in free verse that pulled me in from the first page. It explores what it means to lose someone you love from two different perspectives. Brooklyn was Lucca's girlfriend when he died and Nico his brother. Brooklyn's pain is evident right away as she writes letters to Lucca everyday. She hasn't been able to fully grieve Lucca's death and it feels like maybe she's just not ready to move on. When her friend Gabe dies, Brooklyn begins having nightmares with Gabe chasing her. Gabe's death also begins to affect Lucca's brother, Nico. Only, Nico isn't seeing Gabe, he's receiving messages from Lucca to help Brooklyn. The only problem is Nico hasn't really grieved himself and hasn't spoken to Brooklyn since Lucca died. Despite not knowing how he was going to do it, he decides to listen to Lucca and sets out to help Brooklyn as best he can. Chasing Brooklyn is poignant and well written. I loved reading a book in this writing style and found it very easy to read. The characters stories stayed with me even after I'd finished reading and I have since been back to it to read excerpts from some of my favorite parts. The emotions Brooklyn and Nico display are realistic and haunting. Having never read anything by the author before, I was pleasantly surprised with how much I loved this book. It's definitely going on the top shelf with my other favorites.

Woah. Just... Sigh . Wow. Crooked Kingdom was FANTASTIC. I know that's pretty contradictory to my opinion of the first book Six Of Crows, which I didn't like too much, but saints, did I love this book. Crooked Kingdom just did it for me. While I didn't enjoy Six Of Crows too much this one just blew me out of the water. Okay, so I'm going to get to the reviewing so I'm first going to do no spoilers and then I'll put a disclaimer when I'm going to start talking about spoilery parts. So from now on, no spoilers for either of the books. So this books follows the aftermath of the crews plan to break into the Ice court and retrieve Bo Yul-Bayor. If you read it, we all know how it goes down but for the sake of not spoiling anyone we won't talk about that. This is very much a story of trying to avenge their losses and tie off any loose ends of the story that were left open. We are on a journey of revenge and defeat with these characters and we learn so much about every single one of them throughout the book. So much is revealed to us and I love the way the story unravels as we near the end. The writing was fantastic and imagining these scenes in my head was just so vivid thanks to Leigh Bardugo's awesome skill at creating such imagery and portraying it all through her words. But now let's talk about one of the most exciting parts-the characters. Okay so anyone who has read this duology will understand what I mean when I say THESE CHARACTERS ARE JUST SO PRECIOUS AND PERFECT AND I LOVE THEM SO DAMN MUCH. They were all just written so perfectly and I love the story behind each of their lives. They are all my favorites, to be frank, and I couldn't pick out a top three if you payed me to. One thing I love so so much about each and every one of the characters was how they all had a distinctive feature or quirk that just made the character them and their own. Lets take Kaz, the seemingly heartless Barrel boss- with his gloves, because of his inability to bear the touch of skin to skin contact. Or his cane or his personal vendetta against you-know-who-if-you-read-it. Then Jesper, with his revolvers and his whole background with his family and where he grew up. Can't forget Inej, with her knives and acrobatic skills and her family history. And Nina, who has a food fetish and who we all know to be a Grisha from day one, yet we don't know the whole story surrounding her relationship with Matthias. Matthias, with his past as a drA1 4skelle, his love for his wolves and his history with Nina. And finally, Wylan, who has a dirtbag of a father and his inability to read, yet makes up for it with his Chemistry, drawing and music skills. I JUST LOVE THEM ALL SO MUCH. They are probably one of my favourite fictional squads, besides the inner circle in ACOMAF of course and they all just have so much to offer in one way or another and they just put their all into what's presented to them and I LOVE THEM SOOOOO MUCHHHH. I love how all of their stories are revealed slowly and we get a real view of their pasts and how it affects the present to them. I LOVED ALL THE SHIPS AND EVERYTHING OMG. Kaz was just epic though, like just when you thought everything was about to crash and burn before your eyes, Kaz pulls another trick from up his sleeve. That man is just everything. The relationships between all the characters were amazing too like Inej and Jespers friendship and everyone else's its just amazing. They all just go perfectly together I don't know how Leigh Bardugo did it. I just love my little Inej, the spy acrobat, Kaz, the tough merciless Dreg, Matthias, the big meaty druskelle, Jesper, the sharpshooter with a deep-seated secret past, Nina, the food-loving Grisha who loves to flirt with everyone and Wylan, our little scientist. Just GO READ THIS BOOK YOU WONT REGRET ITTT. It will serve you well, I promise. Okay, so by this point I hope you have been swayed enough to go read this duology, and if not for the first book, then for this book. Because these characters and this plot and just EVERYTHING about this book will stick with you for a long, long time. I know this, and I've only just finished this book less than five hours ago. This is gonna take some serious recovery. So this is your cue to leave if you haven't read Crooked Kingdom because I will be talking a whole lot of spoilers for those who have read it so I can vent. Read on at your own risk D DISCLAIMER SERIOUS SPOILERS Okay, let's talk about some key events that took place in this novel. FIRST Learning about the fact that Wylans mother has been alive the whole time....JUST, No. I was so angry at Van Eck like I literally wanted to squeeze the life from him myself ifnrpognd. And when we all thought the final plan was going to get completely ruined at the Auction, but then Leigh was like "HAH, YOU THOUGHT," and then cracked me into a million tiny fragments of bone and flesh, kinda like that scene where Nina controlled those bone relic blanket things. And when we all thought Inej was about to die when she fell off the high wire after Dunyasha showed up but then she didn't because Nina started controlling the dead and got them to chase away the Dime Lions AND set up a net for Inej. LOL, and when Jesper unknowingly kissed Kuwei and we all just got that second hand SHAME. And when Kaz was replacing Inej's bandages and he like freaked out. And in chapter 18 when everything was just going WRONG, but then of course Kaz swooped in with another one of his schemes. And when they framed everything on Van Eck and managed to FAKE A FREAKIN' PLAGUE AND KUWEI'S DEATH. JUST WHAT IN THE WORLD! Sigh . But, we can never forget the part that probably tore even our remains to shreds when Matthias died. Saying that still feels weird because I refuse to believe it. I was just sobbing unceasingly for hours. And how he knew he needed to see Nina again so he tried to cover up the wound and just ran into her arms. And when Nina was screaming for help and no one was there it was like the world itself had turned on them and it just tore. me. to. pieces. Then Inej ran up and was like "let him go," and Nina was like "I can't" and then Inej was like "You will meet him again in the next life. But only if you suffer this now." And then Nina- " 'In the next life then,' she whispered. 'Go.' She watched his eyes close once more. 'Farvell,' she said in Fjerdan. 'May Djel watch over you until I can once more.'" AND THEN THE CHAPTER JUST ENDS. LIKE I WANT TO JUST CRY SO HARD THINKING ABOUT IT. AND THEN MATTHIAS' LAST CHAPTER "Matthias was dreaming again. Dreaming of her. The storm raged around him, drowning out Nina's voice. And yet his heart was easy. Somehow he knew that she would be safe, she would find shelter from the cold. He was on the ice once more, and somewhere he could hear the wolves howling. But this time, he knew they were welcoming him home." That just gave me CHILLS. FULL. BODY. CHILLLLSSS. We saw how his death impacted everyone and when Wylan was saying how they were "All meant to stay standing." It showed them that life can be cruel and unfair but then we see at the end how most of them get their happily forever after. But we don't see exactly how it ended for Nina. She said to Inej, "I won't rest until he does," and how she said that she would bury him herself and everything was just so depressing. I couldn't imagine her pain. But, the way it ended for her just made me wonder if we might get a novella or something. I know we found out a lot about Nina and Matthias' relationship over the course of these two books, but I feel there's more that's been left untold and more that there will be to Nina's future. I picture Nina spending the rest of her life in the comfort of Ravka, surrounded by her fellow Grisha, remembering her great journey with the Dregs and Inej and Matthias and the whole crew. I picture her never getting married to anyone else As sad as that may sound and waiting her for death to take her away to be with Matthias anew. OH! And when Inej said she wasn't done with Ketterdam and how she and Kaz HELD FREAKIN' HANDS! AND THEN HE GOT HER HER SHIP AND BERTH AND FOUND HER PARENTS. AND THEN INEJ WANTED KAZ TO MEET THEM AND HE NODDED AND THEN WAS LIKE "Wait, is my tie straight?" ARHHGH. Like this just gives me so much hope for the two and same with Jesper and Wylan and everyone but arhghg. I think I said most of what I felt and my heart is just so heavy right now but let me know what you thought so we can talk about this, because it's worth talking about. Sigh, sigh sigh Let me know your experiences with this book while I go and grieve.

I mostly just liked seeing how Queen Mabh, Fennrys Wolf, the fae lord of the Spring Court, and all of the other typical mythological figures the characters from Shakespeare's A Midsummer Night's Dream would fit into the story. Kelley gets thrown into the role of Queen Titania in A Midsummer Night's Dream and is wandering around Central Park practicing her lines when she runs into a Sonny. He's one of the Janus Guard who protects the mortal realm from escaped fae and there's a portal in the park that's set to open soon. Then most of the characters from Shakespeare's play turn out to be real and Kelley finds out she's more or less a faerie princess . I had a hard time getting into the whole story, though. And the names were a bit cringeworthy... I'm sorry but "Sonny" is not going to sound like an awesome male lead no matter what he does. And "Tyffanwy" just made me laugh. I think I would have liked this book a lot more in middle school because it's not bad!! Just definitely a "younger" YA book.

Obwohl ich auf dieses Buch unglaublich gespannt war, musste es doch sehr lange auf meinem SUB liegen, bis ich es endlich in die Hande genommen habe. Leider hat sich das Buch fur mich als kleine Enttauschung entpuppt, denn leider wurden meine Erwartungen nicht erfullt. Der Schreibstil ist an sich ganz gut, allerdings konnte mich die Autorin leider gar nicht an das Buch fesseln. Die Charaktere und Orte wurden nur recht oberflachlich beschrieben, was wirklich schade ist, denn besonders Avalon wirkt unglaublich interessant und ich hatte gerne so viel mehr erfahren. Obwohl man der Autorin anmerkt, dass sie sich mit ihrem Werk Muhe gegeben hat, wirken die Charaktere doch stellenweise sehr lieblos. Es fehlt ihnen an Tiefe und auch die Beschreibungen sind mir oftmals nicht detailliert genug gewesen, sodass ich mich nur schwer in sie hineinversetzen konnte. Wirklich schade, denn das Potential ist vorhanden. Besonders Dana wollte ich unbedingt ins Herz schliessen, weil ich finde, dass sie es bereits viel zu schwer im Leben hatte Ihren Vater hat sie nie kennen gelernt, ihre Mutter ist eine Alkoholikerin, die ihr das Leben stets schwer macht und sie selbst mochte einfach nur ein normales Leben fuhren. Leider erschien sie mir dann doch an vielen Stellen unsympathisch und unreif, da sie oftmals sehr murrisch und schmollend erschien, was so gar nicht zu ihr passen wollte. Ich konnte mich jedoch teilweise in sie hineinversetzen, wenn es um die Suche nach dem Vater und der Suche nach sich selbst ging, jedoch konnte ich ihre Entscheidungen zum Grossteil nicht verstehen und somit fiel es mir oftmals schwer, sie zu mogen. Gleiches gilt fur ihre Tante, sowie Ethan und Kimber, bei denen man sich nie sicher sein kann, ob man ihnen vertrauen kann oder nicht. Naturlich muss es in so einem Buch auch eine Liebesgeschichte geben, allerdings endet diese auch wieder recht schnell, da das Vertrauen von Dana missbraucht wird. Diese wird jedoch recht kitschfrei erzahlt und durch zaghafte Anfange wirkt diese auch recht authentisch, sodass ich hier nicht genervt die Augen verdreht habe. Interessant sind die politischen Umstande in Avalon, die ein grosser Bestandteil der Geschichte sind. Mann kann niemanden vertrauen und niemand kann so wirklich sagen, wer das Beste fur Avalon mochte und wer nicht. Interessant ist dabei auch, wie sehr um die politische Macht gekampft wird und es ist stellenweise erschreckend, wie weit einige dafur sogar gehen. Die Covergestaltung ist wunderschon und passt bestens zum Titel. Die Rosenblatter und das Covermodel wirken stimmig, sodass es ein schones Gesamtbild abgibt. Auch die Kurzbeschreibung liest sich gut und hat direkt Lust auf mehr gemacht. Insgesamt bin ich von "Rosendorn" leider enttauscht. Die Handlung ist zwar an sich ganz okay, aber leider nichts, was langfristig im Gedachtnis bleibt. Auch die Charaktere hatten ein bisschen mehr Tiefe vertragen konnen. Schade, aber ich hoffe, dass mich der zweite Band - falls er ubersetzt wird - besser in den Bann ziehen kann.

This book was... not that great. And when I say not that great, I mean horrendous. It definitely had the middle book syndrome. Not to mention a bit of too much emphasis on the poetry for my tastes. Cassia seems to want Ky just because he's the forbidden fruit. There really doesn't seem to be anything about him that she likes except for the fact that he taught her to write. Mmmmmkay. So that's what we're basing love on now? I was not impressed... I also find it a little odd that if it weren't for Ky's point of view being included in the book, there really would be nothing, and I mean NOTHING to read about except walking through a canyon and fields and other such super exciting activities yes, I'm being sarcastic . Now the biggest thing that got me so infuriated I actually thought I was going to throw this thing out the window? The fact that the editing of this book was so incredibly sloppy. I understand that books take time and effort to edit. I get that, I really do. I'm not usually a hard ass about that sort of thing because I know people make mistakes and aren't perfect. I actually enjoy a little bit of imperfection in my books. However, when I am reading a sentence and come across the word "thsee" instead of these I simply want to lose it. This is a paperback which means more people have looked at this error and MISSED IT than is reasonable. Or worse, knew about it and chose to ignore it. Spell check anyone?! Yeah, I know, ain't nobody got time fo dat... Mmm hmm... Really, the only good thing I have to say about this book is that the cover matches nicely to the first one.

Eu digo que e triste, por que me emociona o forca que ela tem que ter para a enfrentar o mundo, e lutar sozinha para na murchar de vez. E maravilhoso, Serio! Essa parte do livro, e uma licao de vida! "-- Quer saber por que voce nunca foi capaz de me fazer chorar? -- perguntei. -- Porque voce tenta derrubar alguem que ja esta tocando o fundo. Nao pode me fazer sentir pior sobre mim do que ja me sinto. E patetico ... " Vale a pena mil vezes! 4.25 stars Right off the bat I feel compelled to say that I have been a blog reader for many years, not just book blogs, which came more recently, but many years ago I started reading "healthy living" blogs, cooking blogs, fitness blogs, and the occasional "mommy" blog. Don't Call Me Baby very much lives in the kind of blogs that I enjoy reading so I'm not the objective source to be able to say that you'll enjoy this book if you're not familiar with these styles of blogs. However, I think there is enough to this book to make it enjoyable no matter your blog background. Because I'm familiar with these blogs I actually think I'm a tougher critic and I give lots of credit to Gwendolyn Heasley for creating an authentic blog world. Imogene's mom is a mommy blogger and has been blogging about Imogene since she was a baby and before that she was a "healthy living" blogger , her mom even let her blog readers vote on Imogene's name. When Imogene was a baby this was ok, but now that she's fifteen and going into ninth grade she's had enough. Imogene feels like her privacy is constantly being violated with her mom posting pictures of Imogene just rolled out of bed, the news of Imogene's first period, and speculation about which boy Imogene will attend the big ninth-grade dance with. And really, it's hard to argue with Imogene's opinion when you hear the evidence. When Imogene's English teacher assigns a project where each student needs to create their own blog and maintain it throughout the year, Imogene, and her best friend Sophie, whose mom also has a blog, are horrified by the idea. The girls eventually decide to make their own blogs called "The Mommy Bloggers' Daughters" where they tell their own version of their lives. Each chapter of the book opens with a post from Imogene's mother's blog and Imogene and Sophie's blogs. I can't really speak to the authenticity of Imogene and Sophie's blogs, but I fell head over feels for Imogene's mom's blog. From the linking back to other posts, to the shout-outs to sponsors, to the trying to get readers to participate in discussion, it read so much like the real-life blogs I read it was good creepy. I'll admit I try to read blogs that are slightly less annoying than Imogene's mom's, but all of the elements were there to make her blog seem authentic. As much as I loved the blogging aspect of the book the family dynamics were my favorite part and left me wanting to run out and read Gwendolyn Heasley's other books ASAP and I've since read Where I Belong and really enjoyed it . When I first started reading I thought Imogene's mom must be a single mom, but she's not, Imogene's parents are married and her dad is very much present, even though he mostly defers to her mom on major decisions like what her mom will feature on the blog. The story of Imogene's parents and her mom's blog is complicated by the fact that her dad's architecture business is suffering during the recession and her family increasingly relies on her mom's blog for money. Even though I wished Imogene's dad would stand up to her mom more I still very much liked him, but my favorite family member was Imogene's grandma, Hope. Grandma Hope was amazing. She lives with Imogene and her parents, but she's very much independent. She grills her own food, she shuns technology like the internet, and she's a championship golfer. Plus she's incredibly wise and ridiculously funny. The journey and growth that Imogene's family underwent over the course of the book was so interesting and relatable, I came to really care for her family, even her boundary-defying mother. In many ways I was reminded a lot of the families in Lindsey Leavitt's books and that is very high praise. Before I read Don't Call Me Baby, the lovely Estelle kept telling me that the main character is very young and obviously Estelle was right. I knew from the beginning of the book that Imogene was fifteen and just going into ninth grade, which is much younger than most of the characters that I typically read about. Throughout the book there would be things that Imogene did or said or things that happened at school that gave me pause and made me wonder what was wrong with these people, but then I reminded myself that the characters and young and that fifteen year olds have stupid fights and make up quickly and make silly decisions. With that in mind, I also really enjoyed the subplots about Imogene's friendship with Sophie and how that relationship grew over the course of the book. Imogene also has a crush on a boy and I loved how he wasn't always perfect and how Imogene was willing to stand up to him when he said or did something that bothered her. Bottom Line I could go on gushing about this book for many more paragraphs, but I'm going to cut myself off now and say that this a great book. The questions about technology and the information we and other people put out there were fascinating and thought-provoking and the family and friend relationships were dynamic and true-to-life. Even though Don't Call Me Baby features younger characters than I'm used to it's just further proof that if the story, characters, and writing are there age is only a number. Perfect. All I have to say. I just finished it about 10 minutes ago, so I will edit this review later to say some more thoughts. It's not for everyone, and I can see why other people don't like it, but in my view, it's just perfect. There are...kind of spoilers...not major ones, but I would read the book before this review. Okay, now I'll try to write a real review. But this is going to be hard... All right...I'll start with what I didn't like. 1. Gale. His character gets kind of ripped off in Mockingjay. Yes, he gets more face time, and I have a sense of what drives him what he went through with District 12...gotta suck , but I don't really have any idea why he "loves" Katniss, if indeed he does at all. He's accepting of the fact that Katniss won't be able to love him while Peeta is being held by the Capitol, but that in itself is out of touch with what little we know of his character. Isn't he supposed to be the one driven by "fire", as Katniss herself puts it? Shouldn't he put up more of a fight for Katniss? And towards the end...he gets a "fancy job" up in District 2, and...we never hear from him again. I feel like he should have been given more of a chance. 2. Well...actually, that was all I really disliked about it. Although...actually, one quick question Does anyone know Katniss's mother's name? Do we ever find out? I feel like she should have gotten a name... Things I like and feel I must defend . 1. Katniss. Okay, people have been complaining about Katniss in this book that she had no strength or fire. I've gotta disagree on that. She is fighting just as hard in this book as she fought in Hunger Games and Catching Fire. She's just fighting in a different way--towards a different goal. In The Hunger Games, it was for survival and to protect her family in the Games. In Catching Fire, it was the same--just a little more was at stake. In Mockingjay, she's fighting for Peeta. And for herself, I think. She just wants to know who to fight for, and I think Collins overlooked that this mental struggle would leave room for little else, like bombing and shooting things, which other people seem to take as Katniss's strength. I think the mental struggle in this book is just as important as shooting other people was in the first two books. It's a mind vs. body thing--we all know Katniss can kick ass at archery etc. But we don't know how she puts up with the opposite kind of pressure--the pressure from the rebels and from Peeta's instabilities. And no, she doesn't handle it all that well, but hey. Collins made her human, not some kind of robot. She's allowed to crack a bit, even if we all get frustrated with her sometimes. I don't know if this makes any sense--I'm scared to reread it, because I think I might have contradicted myself or repeated myself...sorry, guys, bear with me. 2. Everything else. I just really liked this book. Yes, Gale didn't get a fair chance--but whatever, I was for Peeta anyways. I think Collins outdid herself on this one. The writing is a bit choppy at points. And Collins couldn't have satisfied everyone. I think this was about as good as a conclusion as she could have gotten out of such a monumental series.

S. 272 Inhalt Die Schlacht in der UN hatte ihre Opfer gefordert. Vincent verfallt nach dem Tod eines seiner Bioten mehr und mehr dem Wahnsinn. Der Rest von BZRK versucht sich zu sammeln. Sadie und Noah, die sich nun Plath und Keats nennen, nahern sich nach den gemeinsamen Erlebnissen an. Doch eine gemeinsame Mitte konnen sie noch nicht finden. Dennoch sind Gefuhle fureinander vorhanden. Auch die Gegenseite ist nicht untatig. Bug Man steuert durch seine Verdrahtung die Prasidentin der Vereinigten Staaten. Diesen Mord konnte er nicht verhindern. Doch von einer Sekunde auf die andere befindet auch er sich in ziemlicher Gefahr! Der Krieg auf der Nanoebene entwickelt sich weiter. Der technische Fortschritt verlauft rasant und bleibt hoffentlich kontrollierbar. Aber kann man diese Wesen wirklich im Zaum halten? Die Lage spitzt sich zu. Dann gibt es da noch dieses ,,Puppenschiff". Doch es ist nicht so niedlich, wie der Name vermuten lasst... Meinung Es ist noch gar nicht so lange her, dass ich den ersten Teil ,,BZRK" gelesen hatte. Die Grundidee und die Umsetzung gefielen mir richtig gut und so durfte es nicht lange dauern, bis der zweite Teil bei mir einziehen konnte. ,,BZRK reloaded" habe ich nach dem Einzug deshalb auch nicht lange liegen lassen konnen. Es ist ja immer spannend zu sehen, ob eine gute Umsetzung einer nicht alltaglichen Idee auch in einem zweiten Teil fortgefuhrt werden kann. Gleich zu Beginn kann ich auf jeden Fall sagen, dass ich definitiv nicht enttauscht wurde! Die Geschichte selbst setzt nahtlos an den ersten Teil an. Die Charaktere waren mir sofort wieder vertraut. Ich erlebte einen vollig desorientierten und depressiven Vincent, dessen Zustand sich wahrend der Geschichte nur wenig bessert. Doch wie aus dem Nichts zeigt auch er plotzlich und uberraschend wieder einige Starken, auch wenn diese nicht direkt in seiner Person selbst zu begrunden sind. Jedenfalls ist er ein wichtiger Baustein fur den Fortlauf der Geschichte und spielt eine grosse Rolle fur die Gruppe rund um BZRK. Sadie und Noah verflechten sich in so manchem kleinen Geplankel. Fast ware es tatsachlich passiert, denn immerhin fuhlen sie sich sehr zueinander hingezogen, doch ein Notfall verhindert die letzte Konsequenz. So bedauerlich dies auch ist, besinnt sich Noah letztendlich auf seine Aufgabe. Denn immerhin hangt Sadies Leben davon ab. Nachfolgend werden die Gelegenheiten weniger, der Beziehung selbst schaden diese Momente jedoch nicht. Sadie, nun Plath genannt, zeigt fortwahrend wachsende Starke. An Selbstbewusstsein scheint es ihr nicht zu mangeln. Die ihr gestellten Aufgaben lost sie fast muhelos, dabei hat sie aber immer ein Auge auf den Weg von Noah bzw. Keats. Die beiden Schicksale wurden gut miteinander verwoben, wobei jeder seinen eigenen Weg dabei immer im Blick hat. Noah bzw. Keats versucht immer wieder, aus dem Schatten von Sadie auszubrechen. Doch seine Gefuhle zu ihr sind viel zu gross, als dass er es tatsachlich schaffen konnte. Dennoch zeigt er in den wichtigsten Situationen seine Starken und bringt sie gewinnbringend an. Auch wenn dieser Charakter ein klein wenig in den Hintergrund gerat, erlebte ich Noah genau an den richtigen Stellen als prasent und hilfreich. Auch Bug Man gibt nun mehr von sich preis. Er ist letztendlich nicht nur ein knallharter Twitcher. Nein, auch hinter seiner Fassade stecken menschliche Gefuhle, die er ab und an offenbart. Er spurt selbst, in welch grosser Gefahr er schwebt und versucht, das Richtige zu tun. Nur wird ihm sein Handeln hier noch helfen konnen? Michael Grant schreibt seine Geschichte in gewohnt flussigem Schreibstil. Er verzichtet dabei auf uberdetaillierte Darstellungen, bleibt dennoch in dem Beschriebenen sehr vorstellbar. Die Handlungsstrange gewinnen insgesamt definitiv an Komplexitat und neue Charaktere tauchen auf der Bildflache auf, die sehr gut in die Geschichte eingebaut wurden und ihr mitunter eine andere Sichtweise bescheren. Der Plot wird in Vergangenheitsform aus verschiedenen Sichten erzahlt. Vor allem bringt der Autor dieses auf den ersten Blick normal wirkende ,,Puppenschiff" mit ins Spiel, das nach dem ersten Kennenlernen aus meiner Sicht die Holle sein muss, auch wenn es die Bewohner mitunter gar nicht so empfinden. Die Handlungsstrange selbst laufen selbsterklarend aufeinander zu, und finden letztendlich auch zu einem gemeinsamen Ziel. Einem Ziel, das man so mit Sicherheit nicht erwartet hatte. Im Endeffekt hatte ich mit ,,BZRK reloaded" ein definitives Lesevergnugen. Michael Grant konnte mich mit seiner Welt aus Sicht von Nanobots und Bioten dermassen fesseln, dass ich das Buch kaum aus der Hand legen konnte. Zielsicher fuhrte er mich durch die von ihm geplanten Aktionen und lange wusste ich nicht, wohin mich dieser Weg bringen wurde. Der Autor steigerte seine Geschichte bis hin zu einem grossen Finale, liess die Handlung dann nach und nach beruhigend ausklingen und hat ein Ende gewahlt, das mich den nachsten Teil formlich herbeisehnen lasst. Furs Erste wurde ich jedoch mehr als zufrieden zuruckgelassen und ich bin schon gespannt, was sich Michael Grant fur ,,BZRK - Apokalypse" alles einfallen lassen hat. Urteil ,,BZRK reloaded" ist eine eindeutig gelungene Fortsetzung, die mich permanent an die Seiten gefesselt hat. Ich komme gar nicht umhin, dieser eindrucksvollen und nachvollziehbaren Geschichte 5 Bucher zu vergeben. Fur alle, die sich von den womoglich alltaglich umgebenden Gefahren nicht beeindrucken lassen, in fremde Gefilde eintauchen konnen und eine spannende Geschichte nicht verschmahen. An ARC of this title was provided by the publisher in exchange for an honest review. My first ARC review. I'm soo excited, and happy that I was able to get an early copy of Marie Lu's new book, The Young Elites. I mean, the Legend trilogy was a great read, one that I immensely enjoyed. To say I was overjoyed to receive this, is an understatement. First of all, I'd like to say that I rate books based on how well I enjoyed the story, not on writing techniques, etc. One last thing, I have no idea how to do this, so if you see any mistakes,I'd ask you to forgive me. Moving on, I'll try not to spoil anything. I really enjoyed the concept of this novel. It was a great start. The way Marie Lu crafted these new characters amazed me. Her imagination is wonderful. This is, well, I guess you can call it a dystopian novel? I'm not 100 sure on the correct terminology, but it was set in a different world. One with three moons. That intrigued me quite a bit. The world is full of dangers. Most notably, are the Inquisitors, and The Young Elites, who are at odds with each other. The characters were very unique and I found it refreshing, that not ONE character was perfect. They all had scars, either physical or emotional. Adelina, the main character, had both. I got the sense that I was in Adelina's place. Her pain was my pain. She quickly became my favourite character, after Raffaele, of course. One of my favourite quotes about her, was something Raffaele told Enzo, shortly after meeting with Adelina. "Every single one of her memories is laced with darkness. It is an infection of the mind. Something is very wrong with her. She should have manifested early, as a child, but only now has she started to find her power. It has built up inside her, and the energy feels twisted in a way that disturbs me." ARC 84 I also found it simply wonderful that the main character was not averse to killing someone, and neither were the Young Elites. Many YA novels have main characters who despise the fact that they have murdered someone, or will have to, and it starts to get old. But here, the characters were accustomed to it. They did it to further their goals, yes, not just to murder someone. But still. It happened, and no one was all "I killed someone. sob, sob. ". Enzo was someone I most definitely liked. He was interesting, and not at all annoyingly mushy. I love when she first meets him, and how we learn more about him and his troupe of friends, as the tale goes on. "Embellish your flaws," he says softly. "They will turn into your assets. And if you become one of us, I will teach you to wield them like an assassin wields a knife." ARC 57 Teren was someone I immediately took a disliking to. He was just plain awful. I didn't like him at all, and I hated him more and more as the story went on. " I would do anything for you "As you command, Your Majesty." ARC 60 Awful man. In love with the queen, and, well, I'm not going to spoil it for you. You'll just have to read it when it's out, in less than a week, might I say! Overall, This is an amazing journey, full of Heartbreak, Pain, Betrayal, Misunderstanding, and more. It's a journey for someone who has come to grow into their own. " I am tired of losing. I am tired of being used, hurt, and tossed aside. It is my turn to use. My turn to hurt. My turn." Daughters Unto Devils was one of my faves from last year, and The Women in the Walls is just not as good. Maybe they rushed Lukavics-that's what it feels like, but this one just doesn't gel and it only has one truly creepy moment. Here's what does work. Lucy is a great narrator. Also the idea of the property. We don't actually get to explore the property perhaps if we had been with Margaret... , but we get that there is something super special about the property. Isolationism Lucy is homeschooled, has zero friends, and apparently no contact with the outside world. She does not act like a modern girl except for binge-watching movies with her cousin. What does Lucy do all day? She has no hobbies. Here's what does not work the time period. It's modern times? I have no idea. Apparently, Vanessa helps Lucy google the history of the house, but the girls do not act like modern teenagers AT ALL. The club. WTF? I really thought we were going for a Rosemary's Baby vibe here and that the club was at the center of it all. I used it, in my mind, to excuse the completely unbelievable behavior of the father. My love for Cate Tiernan's Immortal Beloved caught me quite unexpected last year and that the sequel turned out to be equally engaging and lovely surprised me just as much. But when I decided to order the Balefire series, some older young adult fiction by the same author, as a one-book-reprint, I had already upped my expectations by a chunky notch. I was prepared to meet not one, but two prickly, paranormal heroines who would worm themselves into my heart like Natasya had done. For the description surely sounds like a darker, witchier, sexier young adult version of Lottie and Lisa A girl from Connecticut, whose father has just died in a car accident and who is now moving in with a strange and otherworldly "voodoo" family friend she had never heard of before, and a young, fun-loving witch living in New Orleans with her Nan cross paths in High School and discover that they have to be identical twins. They get roped into a bizzare story full of magic and fall in love with the same mysterious guy. Well... pre-Immortal Beloved I would have heard and heeded the unmistakable sound of the paranormal warning bells tolling like mad The words "love triange" and "mysterious young man" used together in a blurb by Booklist are something that would have me make a U-turn before even contemplating to add a title to my wishlist under normal circumstances. But a book by the author of Immortal Beloved ... I had been so confident that another miracle would happen and bought the 974 pages in one go. The reward for my unusual optimism have been 131 pages of the most severe, most nauseating and most disturbing case of double instant-love I have ever come across. After having read myself through quite a share I did not really believe that surpassing the lowest of low would be possible. But it was. After one drink on a lumpy love-seat in a dark bar Girl One Clio is "totally, completely, 100 percent happy", convinced that she has found "the one" she is going to spend her life with and that he is worthy of her love "I know I wanted another margarita and instead got a 7UP, which made me fall even more in love with him. I could trust him." Shortly after, Girl Two Thais falls head over heels in love with the same guy in a beautiful garden next to a hidden church. She admits she is "a little creeped out" by his low voice and his suggestion to leave for his nearby apartment together, but "there was no mistaking it -" she "saw admiration in his eyes. Attraction." And when he says that they will soon meet again, she "knew that he was right". Well. I am going to stop reviewing this now. I still feel a bit queasy.... but also a bit angry at myself. I could have bought my own copy of Pan's Whisper or The Immortal Rules with the money. Alas, back to being a suspicious buyer.

On the eve of Joy's birthday, Joy is terrified Icka will cause her social standing to plummet, but when her family life is suddenly changed, she finds herself needing to reevaluate her abilities, her friendships, and her feelings about Icka before it is too late. I wanted to enjoy this book since the premis of supernatural and unusual abilities interest me, but the writing in the book ultimately failed to meet my expectations. The plot concludes with no real development in the characters or situations and the writing quality lacks the finesse and originality it needs to be a quality example of YA's potential. Although it is an enjoyable read on a surface level, the characters are so simplistic and shallow on emotional level that it is difficult to connect. The book seems to be an attempt at a bildungsroman, but at the end I feel as though little has changed for Joy on a deeper level.

This is normal-ish behaviour for a vampire, don't get me wrong. The thing that bugs me is Bella's reactions to it. This isn't how people are meant to behave around vampires. You're meant to be scared. They're dangerous. They could kill you in an instant. But nope, she's loopy for him. Like at what point do you say, this guy has been watching me sleep at night, this is slightly not okay? 2 - Vampires are meant to be dangerously seductive. Don't get me wrong. I applaud Meyer for reinventing the vampire as she saw fit to do. That's great, it shows quite a bit of imagination what she's done. But it just bugs the living hell out of me. They're not meant to be these sexy, sparkling boys that you want to just sit and watch you no matter what. They're meant to be deadly. Same with werewolves which I'll go into in my review of New Moon . Vampires are meant to be dangerously seductive as I've said. You're meant to wake up and dread that they're in your room, watching you because it means they've chosen you as prey. Even if they've chosen you as a lover, they've chosen you as prey. There isn't any way you're getting out of this alive or human. Vampires are meant to be scary, and this didn't do it for me. Edward's behaviour is severely scary and alarming, and if anyone was doing that to me, I would be calling the cops. This just didn't do it for me. I loved it when I was younger, and after thinking it over, I'm definite that this just isn't the book for me.
