I watched the show without knowing that it's actually an adaption from a book. Naturally, being an avid reader that I am, I waste no time in searching for the book to read it. Despite being a great show, the book somehow is lacking in a lot of areas. It is uncommon for a movie tv show to be better than the books but it has happened and in this case, it happened again. First and foremost, as unusual as it is, the tv show has more character development and depth compared with the book. gasp This is highly disappointing as you'd expect that to be the opposite. Also, as absurd as it sounds, the author had not made an effort to describe her characters or I may have missed it? aside from a select few like Clarke who from all that I've read had gathered that she has "shiny blonde hair that shines from the sunlight moonlight" or Octavia that was mentioned as being chubby and has wide blue eyes. This is quite maddening because this is a novel and descriptions of the characters' features are as essential as the plots itself. If it weren't for the show, I will have no idea what's going on in the story and I will have fits from reading the book! It seems like the tv show completes the book and fills in the missing plots and added in characters that's essential to the show. Somehow, the book felt incomplete in the sense that we weren't told in depth what happened to earth and how exactly were the people in The Ark was sent to space. It would have been better if the book had mentioned and elaborate more in that areas. So we were introduced to a post-apocalyptic world where humans live in space in some sort of a space station called The Ark. We weren't told how they survived in the space station or how exactly they got there in the first place. The settings were bland and nonconstructive in the sense that it is not majorly involve in the story but only serves as an essential background for the story. It became clear after a few chapters that this book is not so much about surviving in a post-apocalyptic world as it is about romance. From early on we were introduced to Wells Jaha the son of the Chancellor who committed a crime that had the potential to endanger the lives of everyone on board The Ark just so he can be with his "one true love" selfish much? . Not that the Chancellor had any problem in sending his only son to an uncertain fate at the earth that could highly potentially kill his son. Despite what Wells had done to be with Clarke his one true "love" , Clarke was not any more appreciative of him than she is with anything else. I can understand that Clarke resented Wells because he did "something" that betrayed her but what I hate about her is that she is so uncertain in making her choice. At first she hate Wells then she make up with him because he saved her from an almost sure death rolls eyes . Ironically, she broke up with him again after that because he was trying to stop her from another certain death by running into the fire to save someone. Guess what she did next? She ran away with another guy. Thus, ensues a love triangle war! In the second book I guess. All in all, The 100 is a bland and boring story that centers mostly around young romance and completely lack of the post-apocalyptic world that I was expecting. I love the show though. It is million times better than the book. I will continue watching the show but I can't say the same for the book.

The best way I can describe my experience with Cat Girl's Day Off would be that it was like having a bad day. A bad day is when you wake up late, drop your toothbrush on the bathroom floor, can't find the car keys, see some young kid screaming in the grocery store, and don't get the last piece of pizza at dinner. Sure, if any of these individual moments happened on a perfectly normal day it wouldn't really matter overall, but on a bad day it's the way the little things add up and build upon each other that makes it so bad. With Cat Girl's Day Off the overall picture is actually very pretty. The main character, Natalie Ng, is so likeable that I was rooting for her almost instantly. Her world of superpowers being less-than super is also just a really great concept for a YA novel. The way Natalie's cat communication abilities played into her personality and the plot worked very well. Something else I would really praise the book for is the attention paid to the social environment of teenagers. The book acknowledges the popular use of blogging, tweeting, and characters actually calling each other without making it feel like a gimmick or dating itself with references that won't work a year from now. Here we get that acknowledgement as well as incorporation in a natural way that makes the story better for it. I would actually compare this book to something like the Mediator series with Shadowland or The Ghost and the Goth books. You have a main character that has this special ability, only here it's cats instead of ghosts, they are then put into a situation where they have to use their secret gift to try and get to the bottom of whatever unnatural event has presented itself at their front door. They are the only one who can help, but they don't necessarily want to stick their neck out. Unfortunately, although I am a fan of these sort of novels where Cat Girl's Day Off goes wrong is that it just doesn't give you enough. It needed more world building, it needed more character building, it needed more urgency, it needed some serious editing, and it needed to be a series instead of a stand alone. Where the book starts off is very promising. We are introduced to Natalie and her family dynamic of being the middle child. She's also half-Chinese, which automaticly earns diversity points and a high five. We then get introduced to her friends Oscar, who is gay Asian, another high five, and Melly who both seem like very interesting companions. All is going well until the mystery kicks in and every character aside from Natalie becomes unrealistic and unbearable. This is where the bad day started. The characters of Melly and Oscar start off pretty good and go down hill fast. Oscar and Melly just don't seem like they're really Natalie's friends. They treat her like a play thing and it's a little condescending the way they act around her. There was never a moment where it seemed like this group even had anything in common. I never understood why she hung out with them, which is a fatal flaw considering most of the book is based around their friendship. Oscar took the brunt of my dislike. He's a lot like Jack from Will and Grace, except not over-the-top funny. There were a lot of smaller moments centred around Oscar that left me wondering what the author was trying to accomplish with this guy. And then there's Melly who was almost completely defined by her looks. Any mention of her centred around how pretty she is or how she's using her attractiveness to get something. This happened on page 40, which was possibly the worst moment in the entire book. Melly is about to use her feminine wiles to distract this guy at the front desk of a hotel so Oscar and Natalie can sneak into the elevator to get to one of the rooms. So, Melly has gone up to this guy who is older then herself with the intent of heavily flirting with him, even though she's only sixteen. This didn't bother me because it's been done before and keeps the plot moving. However, then our main character turns around in the middle of her sneaking to make the point that this guy is a "Dirty old man" because he's smiling and laughing at the attention. This bothers Natalie because she says it's clear Melly "doesn't look a day over sixteen". This is followed up on page 43, with "Melly still has that perv talking to her up at the desk". These two quotes bothered me. It bothered me to the point of complete rage on behalf of the guy. I'll be the first person to point out when some dude is acting creepy or pervy, screw those guys, but let's establish something here. He is not going up to Melly and initiating this sort of behaviour. As far as Natalie or the reader knows he is not touching her, grabbing her, harassing her, demeaning her, acting suggestively towards her, or in any way behaving inappropriately. All anyone sees him doing is smiling and laughing which makes him a both a "dirty old man" and a "perv". This guy was instantly vilified in a way that wasn't at all necessary in the story. It's true that guys should be respectful, but us girls should be expected to do the same, and I did not like the message this was sending about how it was totally fine for her to flirt with him with the intent to manipulate him, but not fine that he responded to it with anything less than "You shall not pass!". Then there were the complete gaps in logic at the climax of the story with unrealistic character behaviour there is this girl who has been held hostage for two years and now that she's free she seems to be totally fine! Not, you know, curled into a ball crying because she had been forced to starve and pee in a bucket. and even more unrealistic excuses in order to drive the plot forward like when Natalie Friends Formerly kidnapped girl dramaticly flee the police because they think they might get arrested for breaking and entering when inside they found a girl chained to f-ing floor who had been held hostage for two years! Also, maybe she should be going to the hospital and not on your crazy adventure ride! or the way Natalie's older sister plays role in the mystery by finding out very important information but never getting around to telling her sister or when she knows her sister is tangled up in this mess but conveniently doesn't ever answer her phone. On top of all that there would also be times when characters would be talking about the present, but using past tense. An example being when Natalie says on 102 "I really hated that guy" when I believe she's talking about how much she hates him in that moment. There were also sometimes words that were a letter off, like on page 100, "I snitched some of the pages". Or the way she says that her crush has the "same eyelashes" as his mother. Or the use of little sayings in place of swear words. "monkey poo" and "flagpole sitter" being two examples. Or how the title never plays a part in the book. Day off from what?! All together this made Cat Girl's Day Off into a painful read that I only finished out of the bazaar hope that things would get better. Throughout the entire story I never lost hope that it might win me back because the potential was there! To get back to something I said above before I burst into flame , I mentioned how I think this should have been a series. This may seem confusing since I didn't like the book, but when you look at the Mediator as a comparison it starts to make a lot more sense. The Mediator series wouldn't have worked as a stand alone because if Meg Cabot had to tie everything up in a nice little bow at the end of Shadowland that story wouldn't have been as good. By opening it up to be a series it left the story with somewhere to go. Cat Girl's Day Off could have benefited from that. Instead we get the most unearned Happily Ever After that I've seen in a while. Now, I know that there will be plenty of people who will love this book, from the description I really did think I would be one of them, but even now I can see how this would still be enjoyable for some people. However, my experience did not do the concept justice. I really wish this could have gone better or maybe more honestly that I had just avoided it altogether.
I am satisfied but not really with the ending...I need more! Overall, this is an amazing book. I would highly recommend.

I so badly wanted to like this book after hearing all the hype that surrounds it and reading so many good things said about it, but I just didn't. Juliette is probably one of the weakest protagonists I've read in a long time and I would consider it fairly difficult to be a weak protagonist in a dystopian novel. The fact that she was a weak female protagonist irritated me all the more. She was one-dimensional and her obsession with Adam was ridiculous. It bothered me that female character given so much power could be so weak and reliant on the male characters around her. The fact that the only female characters in the book besides her were also passive, deceiving and or afraid Benny and the other women in Omega Point who shunned Juliette was concerning - there were literally no strong female characters. Also the romance between the Juliette and Adam was unrealistic, bordering on farcical. In terms of character development or complexity, the only character that seemed to have any depth was Warner, he was one of the few characters I actually enjoyed reading about, along with James and Kenji. I also enjoyed the more dramatic scenes such as the scene where Juliette and Adam escape the military base as I thought the writing described the chaos really well. I would also have enjoyed a bit more detail in terms of world-building, there were a lot of unanswered questions at the end of the novel, which I guess has the purpose of drawing you in for the second book which I may consider reading, if only with the hope of encountering at least one strong female character in the series.

A copy has been given to me by the author for an honest review What a breath of fresh air was this book. So different from most of the others I've read. I loved the development of Tessa's and Morick's relationship. The fact that it wasn't insta love made me so glad. I am stuffed full of the insta love. Come on. Nothing is that easy. You have to work for it. I don't believe I've read another book where the characters worked so much for it. The plot was just enough to give a rush but not to overwhelm. I felt that this book was mostly about acceptance and hope and not drama. Of course, there was drama but it wasn't overdone. For which I am so grateful. Beatriz is such a wonderful friend to have. I think that every girl should have a friend like her. She was loyal, and funny, and smart, the best for our Tess. I even loved Brad who was a very nice side character and brought more depth to the story. I am so so so so so happy that there weren't any love triangles or rectangles. I am sick of that. But I was also amused by the slight jealousy from Morik. He was so CUTE. All the gestures, the small touches, the handmade gifts. All was a welcome reprieve. I enjoyed reading this book so much and I recommend it for whoever wants to read something not disturbing for a change It is a easy and fun read. Thank you Ms. Haag, you're awesome!

A modern day fairytale with that old world feel The Darkest Part of the Forest takes place in a modern town bordered by a forest full of fey. Its quite the hot tourist attraction what with the ageless young horned boy that lies asleep in a glass coffin in the woods. But the townspeople know that the fey can be dangerous and as they've lived alongside them for years they always take precautions that the tourists never do. Something has been changing though because not only are tourists being preyed upon by the fey but now townsfolk as well. Kiss the boys and make them cry Hazel is a bit of a heart breaker. She likes to have fun and she isn't opposed to trysting with the boys at parties with a few heated kisses. But she never wants anything more then that...except maybe she does and is too afraid to go after the one boy she shouldn't want...her brother's best friend Jack. The musician who refuses to make music When Ben was just a baby his artist mother was painting in the woods and met a fey lady who bestowed a blessing curse of music upon Ben. The gift was that of music - to be able to enrapture anyone that listens. But all gifts from the fey are double edged. Of both worlds and neither Jack is a changeling who grew up in the town of Fairfold as if he were any normal human boy - except in his case everyone in town knows he is a changeling. His foster mother realized as soon as he was swapped for her own child that she wasn't the baby she had given birth to and thus hatched a plan to get her baby back but when she did she refused to give up Jack saying that any mother who would willingly leave her child doesn't deserve them and so she raised both babies as her own. Be careful what you wish for This book revolves around Hazel 16 and her brother Ben 17 . Mostly though this is Hazel's story. She's always held this childhood dream of being a knight ever since they were children playing in the woods that surround their town of Fairfold and discover a half eaten body by the lake. A nasty hag attacks Hazel and with the help of Ben and a sword Hazel finds they are able to put an end to the nasty water hag. From then on Hazel is determined to protect the people from harm. But she and her brother were in more danger then she wanted to admit and Ben soon puts a stop to their adventuring because of his mounting worry. But Hazel doesn't ever want to stop - so she makes a bargain...now flash forward about 6 years... Your debts are coming due The horned boy in the glass coffin is missing and Hazel's debt to the fey for her bargain has come due. Her and her brother who have both been in love with the horned boy since they were children are set on finding and helping him and enlist the help of Ben's best friend Jack. Magical, engrossing and a YA fantasy definitely not to be missed The Darkest Part of the Forest was all around fun. At times dark and foreboding with parts that made me ache with sadness to others that were full of magic - the story did a fabulous job of embodying a true fairytale while placing it in a modern setting. I've really enjoyed everything I've read thus far by this author. She has such a smooth and easy writing style that had me flying through the pages and at the end before the day was through. The characters were dynamic and the story didn't seem to suffer any of the typical YA tropes that frequently plaque some of the other YA books I've read. If you are a lover of fairytales this right here is the book of goodies you want.

Aku awalnya tidak menyangka bahwa Tablo sudah menulis sebuah buku. Mungkin sama seperti sebagian besar pembaca dan penikmat musik di luar sana,aku pertama kali mengenal Tablo sebagai salah seorang anggota dari grup hip-hop terkemuka Korea Selatan dibawah naungan YG Entertainment yaitu Epik High.Sebagai seorang penggemar,aku mengakui bahwa Tablo adalah seorang penulis lirik yang brilian.Lirik demi lirik dalam berbagai lagu yang ditulisnya memiliki makna yang mendalam dan membuatku jatuh hati.Aku adalah salah satu penikmat musiknya. Aku sudah menjadi penikmat musik Epik High dan Tablo untuk beberapa waktu ketika aku menemukan buku 'Pieces Of You' di salah satu toko buku.Waktu itu aku sedang mencari-cari buku untuk dibaca selama liburan. Mendadak pandangan mataku terfokus pada 4 buku hitam yang tersusun rapi di ujung rak.Nama penulis buku itu ditoreh dengan tinta putih. TABLO Refleks saja,aku langsung menggapai salah satu dari keempat buku itu dan benar. Ternyata memang Tablo dari Epik High yang menulis bukunya ! Sebelumnya, aku pernah mendengar bahwa Tablo pernah menuntut ilmu di Stanford University.Kenyataan ini membuatku menjadi makin penasaran dan memutuskan untuk membeli buku ini. Buku ini terdiri dari 10 kisah pendek karangan Tablo. Masing-masing kisah mengambil latar di Amerika Serikat.Mau tidak mau aku jadi berpikir bahwa cerita-cerita pendek ini didasarkan pada kehidupan yang dilalui Tablo selama hari-harinya di Amerika. Secara keseluruhan,atmosfir kesedihan dan depresi cukup kentara dalam novel 'Pieces Of You'. Kesepuluh cerita yang ada,dengan caranya masing-masing mengisahkan berbagai tantangan dan kegalauan yang dihadapi di masa muda. Walaupun pun baru membaca versi terjemahan kedalam Bahasa Indonesia,sentuhan khas ala Tablo tetap mampu aku rasakan.Aku menjadi penasaran untuk membaca versi asli dalam bahasa sebenarnya. 'Pieces Of You' adalah novel yang dapat nikmati sebagai penghibur dan penggugah setelah melalui hari-hari yang melelahkan.

Katie McGarry's characters have a way of getting under my skin and climbing into my heart without me even knowing it, and this time they did it with a lot of bang. CRASH INTO YOU kicks off with Isaiah refusing to deal with one of his biggest issues and Rachel literally running away from hers. Both set the two on a course that would change the rest of their lives in ways neither saw coming. Isaiah is such a complex, layered character and getting to know him and learning more about who he is as a person was such a great experience. He's loyal and fierce and protective, and it made him an instant favorite of mine. Threaded in with that was his vulnerable side as well, and that he allowed Rachel to see it made me appreciate him that much more. He was surprised by it and it endeared me to him. I hope we get to see more of him as the series progresses. Rachel is a fierce, wounded little thing I and loved her. Meeting Isaiah was the best thing that could have happened to her - and vice versa - even though it took some work to get where she needed to be in her life. But she tackled everything with all she had in her, and how could you not admire her for that? The two of them come from such opposite worlds, and those differences brought out the best in both of them. They contrast off each other perfectly and the fit of them is like a key in a lock. I adored everything about this book. I loved what I learned about the things Isaiah and Rachel had in common, and the details just added more depth to the story. This novel is a rollercoaster from start to finish and it's by far my favorite in the series. Katie McGarry delivers from start to finish and left me wanting more. She's at the top of my favorites on the YA list and I anxiously wait for what she sends our way next. Massive thank you to Harlequin TEEN and NetGalley for the eARC. You guys make my face happy.

spoiler alert Horrifying. Excruciatingly disturbing. And these are underrated terms to describe the atrocities depicted in this book. And yet, I liked this book. I'd say loved, but it wouldn't feel right, would it? Who can love a book depicting such horrors? Who would even read a book describing the horrors endured by a 10-year old abducted by a paedophile? Well, I did, and let me tell you, once you do too, there's no going back. This book will leave you wretched, emotionally. However, the author tackled such a terrifying subject in an incredible way. There is no over-the-line detailing, which I appreciate, as well as the short length of the book. Spreading the pain over too many pages would have been too much. The 4 instead of a 5-star rating is solely due to the ending. No, I wasn't expecting a happy-ending I'm being realistic here- or maybe just really pessimistic . Unfortunately, I do believe in the death freedom theory but I just wished for a different death. This one just didn't seem right, to me at least. Anyway, I would recommend this book to knock down the 'ignorance is bliss' belief . It is a powerful, compelling and poignant one. It is the kind of book which you have to put down to clear your head and get a grip a couple of times but definitely need to finish to have closure.

spoiler alert In the past few months I've been reading the Divergent series by Veronica Roth. This is a YA dystopian trilogy consisting of Divergent, Insurgent and Allegiant and now I'm reviewing three books in one go. Reader's warning this is not a spoiler-free review! I started reading Divergent in December and for the first 100 pages or so, I had a hard time getting into the swing of the story. I thought the set-up was interesting, although I felt like there was little disclosed about the background of the world. Of course, once I got to Allegiant I understood why Almost at the very start the reader is made aware that the protagonist Trish is a Divergent and that that is supposed to be a very bad thing. But for the first three quarters of the book there's hardly any mention of it, instead we follow Trish' adventures during the brutal initiation training at the Dauntless, the fraction she has chosen to be a part of. At first I had a hard time comprehending why anyone would ever choose to become a Dauntless, but as the story progressed I came to understand that for better or worse, the approach of the Dauntless actually fit Trish' personality. I enjoyed the flashbacks of Trish' youth in Abnegation, a division that personally would have suited me a lot better. But I thought Trish' inner dilemma between how she respects her parents and the values taught to her by the Abnegation, but that she can't abide by herself was very interesting. The final part of Allegiant had me on the edge of my seat, even as devastating as the events were. Out of the three books I liked Insurgent less, although I did like reading more about the different factions. I also appreciated the realism. Trish' struggle with her parents' death and her own actions, resulting in her fear to fire a gun felt very genuine. I thought Trish was an amazing character strong, resourceful, brave etc. but there's just no fun in reading about a completely perfect character. Trish has flaws she is stubborn and has a serious case of hero-complex, but that actually makes her far more like-able. And then the cliffhanger... I went back to reread the chapter because it was such a shocker. I don't know how many of you remember M. Night Shyamalan's The Village, but it really reminded me of that. Of course, that movie got mainly very negative reviews while it's one of my favorites. This might also explain why I loved the plot twist in Insurgent while many readers were meh about it. And then came Allegiant. I was warned about this book when I picked it up at my local bookstore that I probably wouldn't enjoy it. So with some trepidation I started reading it, waiting for the other shoe to drop. It never did. I loved the new setting and the more in-depth view of this particular dystopian world. Tobias turning out not being the infallible person that he seemed to be in the previous two books scored a lot of points on the realism front with me. There was a part near the end, when they're contemplating yet another revolution that I was starting to get a little wary and confused about who was in the league with who, but then the story reached it's dramatic climax and I was once again impressed by the serious. At this point I like to make it clear again that this is not a spoiler free review... Trish' death. There was a part of me that hated it in a 'but I'd grown attached to that character' kind of way, but overall brilliant and very fitting ending. It takes quite a bit of bravery to kill of the protagonist of your series and I think Veronica Roth handled it very well. For me, with Trish heroically sacrificing her own life to save her brother, the story came full circle. By finally understanding what a true sacrifice means and acting accordingly, Trish became the Abnegation that was somewhere inside her all along. But as it turned out, it took a Dauntless to get there

I loved this book, and I have always loved it. It is well written, and it contains so many literary elements in it, high school students could read this as an example of novel that is both intriguing and educational.

High school junior Pudge's fascination with famous people's last dying words draws the interest of a the beautiful, wounded Alaska, who lives down the hall at his boarding school. His roommate and a few other bright, quirky classmates who would have probably been bullied outcasts in public school experience make up the other characters in LOOKING FOR ALASKA, John Green's award winning first novel. While I loved the last quotes, I didn't connect to the characters or the plot. I love how John Green has inspired a whole generation of YA readers and the success of THE FAULT IN OUR STARS. He's a tremendous human being for what he did for Esther Earl. Even though I didn't like the book I'm still giving it 2 stars because this book has an audience, and just because I'm not that audience doesn't mean I should give LOOKING FOR ALASKA a completely negative review.

Sebenarnya ide dasar ceritanya cukup menjanjikan batas tipis antara benci dan cinta yang melahirkan rasa takut dan obsesi. Sayang sekali ide tersebut kurang dapat dieksekusi dengan baik oleh Penulis. Marianka dan Rem bertemu kembali setelah enam tahun berlalu sejak terjadi peristiwa traumatis yang mengubah hidup Marianka untuk selamanya. Sayangnya Rem sendiri seperti tidak menyadari masa lalu mereka walaupun alam bawah sadarnya menuntunnya untuk mendekati Marianka kembali. Flashback cerita pun diselipkan untuk sedikit memberi gambaran bagaimana keduanya bisa terhubung. Trauma Marianka datang dan pergi setiap saat dia berada di dekat Rem. Bahkan ketika pola yang sama terulang kembali, entah kenapa gadis itu tidak dapat menghindarinya. Latar belakang peristiwa yang membawa petaka di kehidupan Sang tokoh utama terkesan terjadi tiba-tiba tanpa ada satu proses pendahuluan. Bahkan karakter dasar para tokohnya tidak terjelaskan dimana segalanya terkesan sudah dari sananya. Penyebab Rem menjadi sosok yang posesif sejak kecil tidak diketahui. Keberadaan dua tokoh pendukung, Ameria dan Alex tidak banyak membantu perkembangan cerita. Walaupun memang Ameria yang menolong Marianka saat dia terpuruk, namun keterkaitannya dengan Alex terasa sangat kebetulan. Yang patut dipertanyakan adalah peran keluarga Marianka yang tidak disinggung selama proses penyembuhan trauma gadis tersebut. Alasan Marianka hidup terpisah dari kedua orang tuanya pun juga tidak diketahui. Satu hal yang cukup menggangguku terkait profesi psikiater dan lulusan psikologi yang disinggung di dalam buku ini. Terkesan bahwa psikiater itu lulusan psikologi, padahal sebenarnya tidak. Setting cetita pun tidak diketahui, apakah di Indonesia atau di luar negeri karena tidak ada sesuatu yang khas dan mencirikan lokasi cerita. Sekiranya Penulis bisa kebih menggali karakter para tokoh utama dan memberi pondasi lebih kuat dengan memberikan kisah masa lalu yang sedikit panjang, tentu pembaca akan merasa lebih terkoneksi dengan alur cerita para tokoh tersebut. Over all buku ini mudah dibaca, pemilihan kata dan penyusunan kalimatnya pun cukup mudah dipahami. Aku sendiri menyukai gambar sampul buku ini yang menampilkan sketsa bunga kamelia yang juga menghiasi pergantian bab dan juga tercetak di setiap sudut halaman buku ini. 2,5 untuk Fall.

I really wanted to give this a better rating and review, but sadly I was a little disappointed when I thought this was going to be a new great read. It wasn't. The characters were supposed to be intelligent. I mean, we had an upgraded human and a boy genius scientist. That's supposed to show some kind of intellectual advancement, but it didn't. There was a lot of telling instead of showing how clever they both were. Neither of them showed that through their dialogue or actions and the romance just didn't cut it for me, I'm afraid. The characters just didn't seem to get to know each other properly in any way. I mean, sure, we are told that they're physically attracted to each other, but the scientist only mentions how much he's falling in love with her upgraded mental capacity - not her personality or anything else. The ending was sort of thrown together instead of concluding satisfactorily yes, it says 'to be continued' but there was still no sort of notion that this first instalment was actually properly at an end . As I said, I was disappointed. There was clearly a great premise for a story here, but the characters and crumbling of the story did not meet my expectations. My quest for my next great read must sadly continue elsewhere.

spoiler alert Where to start? I don't think I can put into words how much I loved this book. I didn't want it to end. I'm sorry I had to make this a review with spoilers, I can't help it, it's the only way I can talk about it. This was the perfect ending to a wonderful series. I've been very attached to this series, I've enjoyed every single twist and turn along the way. Love. Intrigue. Politics. Action. Humor. This book picks up right where the last book left off. I won't get into the details of what happens in the book. But here are my thoughts on the main aspects of the story. I'll start by saying that even though I loved both Dimitri and Adrian, and sometimes I felt like I was on both "teams" I did want to see a Rose Dimitri HEA. They were meant to be together. Now that being said... Rose is one of my favorite heroines! She kicks ass, she's loyal to her friends and she's a damn good guardian. She battles with her feelings for Dimitri, thinking he can't love her anymore, while still trying to be with Adrian. I only had one issue with her, and that's how she handled the cheating. I was dying for her and Dimitri to finally get together, but when he said that he loved her but that he wasn't going to take a woman away from a man that he liked and respected, she should've ended things with Adrian and then come back to Dimitri. It took away from their big moment and reunion for me. And then when she didn't come clean to Adrian right away because she still needed his help, that was just wrong. The moment she jumps in front of Lisa to save her, I knew that was coming obviously the book is called Last Sacrifice, so something like that had to happen , and I'm really happy that nobody healed her, but that she recovered on her own and that actually broke the bond and she is now alone in her own body! Her and Lisa deserved that going forward. They can both have their own lives. Dimitri The Russian Guardian God! He is just so sexy! And now that he finally realizes that he can be with Rose, every moment they had together had me holding my breath and my heart beating fast. They were so romantic and emotional! These two totally deserved getting their happy ending. I loved the moment when he killed the strigoi and said to her "Your hair is so beautiful". And of course my favorite quote from the book when Rose says to Dimitri "But I was meant for you". I thought I was going to die! He finally lets lose a bit in this book, and is not as hard on following the rules. Lisa Yes we saw that coming. Of course she was destined to be the Queen, and I'm glad she's grown into her own skin enough to actually pass all the tests on her own. She still has the support of Christian and still gets Rose as her guardian! Adrian This was the only issue I had with the book. Yes, Adrian has issues. He has a lot of growing up to do, and Rose was the person he was leaning on for support maybe too much . He was not Rose's equal, I see that. But he loved Rose and the fact that she cheated on him, didn't come tell him, and then he finds out because she's kissing Dimitri before going into a dangerous situation after Adrian came to her aid. Not cool at all. I still hope to see more of Adrian in the spinoff series, I love him! And I really want to see him happy. I want him to get past his issues and grow as a person, but the hurt that was inflicted on him in this book was unnecessary. I was actually happy to see Adrian's reaction to that whole situation because Rose had to see that her actions hurt him. After something like that there was no way things would be ok between them after. And when he confronted her she couldn't even articulate responses. She disrespected him in the worst way, and he had every right to treat her the way he did. Jill I couldn't have been more shocked to find out she's Lisa's sister! My jaw dropped when she opened the door! I'm curious to see if the spinoff series has anything to do with her, since Victor Dashkov made a reference as to her being important special. And she took the whole thing of finding out who her real father was and being Lisa's sister very well. I thought she would have more problems with that. Tasha I didn't see that coming until they interviewed the Alchemyst. Once we rule out Daniella, I knew it was Tasha, and all the reasons fell into place. I think that summarizes my main feelings for this book. It was amazing! Written perfectly, with so much intrigue, mystery, action, and yes romance. I wish it wasn't a young adult novel so we could've read more about what happened with Dimitri and Rose behind close doors, I'm sure that was amazing! I am looking forward to the spin-off series. I can't wait! I will keep reading anything that relates to this world.

For the life of me I cannot understand the phenomenon of this series. I have read all three for three reasons 1 I am interested in YA paranormal and am intrigued by how authors position the "angel" angle. 2 The covers were beautiful and I am a sucker for a love story. 3 My persistent need hope that this series will eventually redeem itself. Dear Lord no pun intended . But this book was terrible. I am sorry for those of you who enjoyed it or those of you that thought it was bearable. I had to force myself to keep going. The story was a constant repetition of Luce searching for a past self and that era's Daniel, finding that reincarnated self, seeing a past Luce die, and the present Daniel getting there just a tad too late to meet up with her. I swear to you this happens for every chapter besides the Epilogue. I wanted to throw the book against the wall. I have been hoping Miss Kate would redeem her lovers, her writing, her story line, but alas I was disappointed yet again. I don't care about Luce and Daniel. I am not sad for them like I got sad for other heroes heroines. I think the Announcers are the weirdest most convenient entity she employs throughout the first three novels, we lose almost all of the fun characters like Cam, Miles, Arriane, Gabbe, and Roland. And all I read was "Don't leave me yet," "Now I know our love is real," "I will always find you." AND NONE OF IT WAS SHOWN TO THE READER. I am always told about their love story and about how in "lust" they are. I like my cheesy, trashy romance novels and the lust in those, but this is supposed to be an epic YA, sweeping of Heaven and Hell romance. And neither character does it for me. I get Daniel is hot with violet eyes. I get Luce is dark haired, pale skinned, and beautiful in every carnation. But personality wise, relationship wise, I saw nothing intriguing or capturing. I still don't understand the curse. Even though the last two chapters tried to present some sort of "reveal" to the reader. But the problem? The plot didn't directly lead us there. I feel like that information could have been given way before this end. It was sloppy and confusing. And I still never got to see how Luce and Daniel MET. How do you have a love story with no beginning? To somehow gift wrap it along with the "beginning of the Fall" was cheap and didn't make a lot of sense. I am masochistic when it comes to this series so it seems I will be reading Rapture from the library only...I wasted 30 precious ones on the first two loads of fluff . And what was with the Prologue? We never get mention of those people that situation again. More and more open-ended story lines that don't make no damn sense. I commend the author for writing a full-length manuscript and I give many kudos for that. However absurd, writing a novel is arduous, but this was just not good.

spoiler alert This book was kind of disappointing. It definitely did not live up to The Battle of Jericho or November Blues. The thing that really sucks is I bought this book for like 25. In retrospect, one of the things I disliked about this book was how Draper wrote. For one, it was all in third person which was totally unnecessary considering the fact that the POVs changed a lot. I also wasn't a big fan of Arielle or however her name is spelled . I understand that Draper set out to show that there was more than one side to her in Battle of Jericho she was really mean and shallow but she seemed like an excuse to show off some more racial stereotypes. Which leads me to my next complaint s . Almost every character seemed to be dealing with distinct teenage, stereotypical problems and it was very annoying. Kofi he broke his arm in Battle of Jericho and as a result was on pain meds. The only thing is, his arm is healed but he's still been taking the meds because...gasp!...he's addicted to them. Jack a.k.a Crazy Jack I don't even feel like putting up Spoiler Alert. I mean, you might as well know that this Jack guy is a bit crazy and ends up trying to shoot up the school. I guess he's suppose to be scitzo or something. I don't know. But again, an emo, misunderstood stock character. November teen mom. Enough said? Arielle her mom is in an emotionally abusive relationship. And, somewhere in the book, Arielle and her mom find out that Arielle's stepfather left them and took all of his and their possessions with them. This doesn't really make sense I mean, why wouldn't he just kick them out? and again, it is just another example of the stereotype 'My stepfather or father figure is abusive' and blah blah. Jericho he's just always had problems so they're not even worth mentioning. Osrick Strange, quiet boy who keeps getting bullied. Sigh. Olivia She's in a wheelchair and she is also Jericho's girlfriend. I applaud Draper for being open to those with disabilities but really? Can we get a little more...contrived please? Can you say Hallmark movie? It seemed like Draper tried to jam too many teen problems into one book. Supposedly the story is focused on some school shooting but this is more like a subplot. All of the above, is basically all you read about until the last ten pages. And let me tell you, it was all very anti-climatic. I mean, I know that this is a good thing. No one should be the victim of a school shooting. But every single plot in this book was weak, I was expecting that something would at least happen in the end that would improve one of the characters at least one of them. please . All that happened was that Jack decided to shoot the window note the cover while trapping all the main characters inside the classroom and someone I can't even remember who. Osrick, maybe decided to be a hero and talked him down or something. I don't even remember because by that time I was so sick and tired of the moaning and played out stereotypes I just wanted to finish the goshdarn thing. Honestly, it seemed like Draper, while writing this book, was watching TV I'd like to imagine MTV or VH1 since they seem to try to 'relate to adolescents while also being insulting to us 16 Pregnant She was writing, lalalalala and maybe some story popped up about addiction and she thought to herself, "Now THAT would be interesting. Let's put that in here". And on and on. The only thing I can't say that for, is November's situation she already had a baby in November Blues but who knows, maybe that's how her mindset was for that book too? I really disliked this book. Like I said, I didn't like all the jammed in 'problems' and I failed to harbor any sympathy for any of the characters. The main plot the 'shooting' fell wayyyy short and it felt very forced, like Draper threw it in at the end for even more melodrama that the book didn't need. Overall, not one of Draper's best, as in, at all. I am just still upset that I actually bought this. That's the saddest part.

This is Tamora Pierce's first stab at writing first person, not to mention in a journal format I know a lot of people don't think she did well with this and I know it is not a style of hers I am used to, but I honestly felt like it wasn't Tamora Pierce who had written the book, but Beka Cooper. Pierce used the journal as an effective method of creating a realistic world and characters. I personally felt like Beka was really well developed because of the way this was written - just the level of diction that would have been lost if this had been told through first person. Story-wise, I don't think it was Pierce's best, but I definitely don't think that it was one of her worst. I eagerly awaited the second installment.

2.5 stars rounded up to 3 stars. Siege and Storm is the second book in the Grisha trilogy, a story about Alina Starkov -- a teenage Grisha with the power to summon light -- and her struggle to defeat the Darkling in his quest for the Ravkan throne. I thought it was about time I picked up the sequel to Shadow and Bone after a couple years oops! later. I have to say that Siege and Storm suffers from some of the same problems that happened in the first novel, but some things were changed for the better. Overall, my rating was based on what I think of the quality of both the writing and the plot. First, let's talk ladies. We have only one new female character in the story Tamar, who is one half of a fraternal twins set. Tamar kicks ass with a multitude of weapons and is half-Shu, half-Ravkan her mother is Ravkan and a Grisha and her father is Shu . Alina thinks she's cool, so we get flattering descriptions of Tamar she's cool, she's beautiful, she's dangerous, but ultimately we like her. Unfortunately, the same attitudes toward the female characters from the first book remain for the rest of the novel. Genya is so beautiful and, wow, even though she's a backstabber and traitor, Alina still thinks she's so great urgh! but why did she have to be a traitor! - Alina . Zoya is still untrustworthy because she's just too damn hot and snobbish, so obviously she's out to get Alina even though Ravka is in a crisis. Marie and the other female Grisha are all stuck-up a-holes still and Alina can't really trust them because she can be picky with whom she trusts in the Second Army while they try to fight the Darkling? 'Kay. The Queen is also an ugly woman now that Genya isn't there to Tailor her face -- um, okay, so that's all that's necessary for her character? Now let's talk gentlemen. Only two main male characters emerge in this novel Nikolai Sturmhond, second in line to the Ravkan throne, and Tolya, the larger twin brother to Tamar. Nikolai is a cookie-cutter stereotype handsome, charming, sneaky, basically your everyday second prince. He's essentially Prince Harry in book-form. I doubt that Prince William is anything like Vasily though. There isn't much about him that sets him apart from the stereotype he presents, but Bardugo tries to push his ruthlessness on you oh, he might be similar to the Darkling because he is a man who can be a bit cruel! gasp! Tolya is also a bit of a cookie-cutter stereotype tall, strong, silent, intimidating but ultimately not bad, giant. There is barely anything interesting about him. He could basically blend in with Tamar's personality except he doesn't really even have one. Parts of the novel dragged for a ridiculous amount of time like preparing the Grand and Little Palaces for war, travelling to Os Alta and going through the Fold on the Hummingbird and other parts moved along at a steady pace. The pacing in general was a bit all over the place, so it was hard to see where the novel was heading -- which is a bad idea for a second book in a trilogy. The love triangle between Alina, Mal and the Darkling is more ? resolved than before, I suppose. But we get the added joy of a fourth person in there -- Nikolai -- who really has no need to be jumping in to make this a fun ha, lies love rectangle. If that wasn't enough, then we have Zoya flirting with Mal when they make it back to Os Alta. Someone kill me before the third book reveals everyone is horny for everyone else. This love situation does not need to be that complicated. I appreciated that Alina and Mal weren't really a part of that love triangle nonsense that YA seems to get off on in the first novel, but Siege and Storm was like purposefully pushing my buttons with their stupid romance. It took up too much of the novel's plot and shoved the more interesting aspects the search for the firebird, war preparations, etc. to the back-burner. This rift between you two isn't like Frodo and Sam, Alina, so stop being such stupid idiots. Another thing about Alina that hasn't changed from the first novel is that she continues to run her mouth to people of a higher status class than her. She fucking punches a prince and there are no repercussions?! Well, fuck me, this bitch gets out of pretty much every hard situation she's ever gotten into and then nothing happens when she continues to be a stupid idiot. If I were the King, I'd execute her for being an inconsiderate and rude douche. She also snarks the King in her head, thank god for that because he's incompetent. Sorry, he's just been recently poisoned and is still weak, so he can't come to phone right now. Can I take a message? Which, side-note, if he's been said to be weak and about to die, why does Bardugo make him seem like a robust, healthy Christopher Lee when he's in the scene? Finally, we come to the linguistics side of this review. Just a couple things were interesting me, so I decided to look them up. Mainly, Tamar and Tolya's names. It turns out that Tolya is a Russian boy's name, meaning "to the East," and Tamar is a Hebrew name, meaning "date fruit , date palm, or palm tree." Tolya being named Tolya is understandable -- their mother was Ravkan and their father was Shu -- but Tamar given a Hebrew name doesn't make sense. The Shu Han seems to be a Mongolia Northern China in this world I mean, how obvious do you need to be with the word "Han" in the name? , but there aren't that many Jewish people in China and they're mostly all in Western China... And the name meaning doesn't make sense in the context of Tamar's purpose in the novel. Since we don't know much about the Shu Han, I'm just basing it off the information given. So either I'm right and Bardugo made the Shu Han be a Mongolia China of the world, or the Shu Han encompasses more of Western Asia the 'Stans, Middle East and if that's the case, I've gotta say HELL NO to that. Those cultures are all so distinct that they cannot be grouped together like that. Another thing that interested me is that Tamar and Tolya can speak un-accented Shu and Ravkan, but Botkin Os Alta's resident combat instructor and Shu can only speak un-accented Shu. Now, I'm well aware that people learning a second language can have an accent in that language or sound like a native speaker dependent on age of learning, phonemic awareness factors, etc. , but it seems like Tamar and Tolya can speak un-accented Shu and Ravkan because they're halfies. I might be reading into that too much probably am , but it's just something that piqued my interest. Last linguistics note when Mal and Alina pretend to be Suli, they put on what could potentially be a Russian Eastern European accent in the real world. Um, aren't they supposed to be in a fictional version of Russia? So, by default, shouldn't that be their accent? Also, are the Suli supposed to be gypsies? Because if they are, the way they are portrayed sounds a bit offensive to Romani people and their culture... Anyway, I still enjoyed the overall plot of the novel. The writing could use more work is winking the only way the men in your novel flirt, Bardugo? , but the story is what carries the novel.

Going back to my review of "Red Queen" I gave it 3.5 stars, but now I'm starting to doubt the fairness of that rating , I noticed that the first thing I pointed out as a problem was Mare - the MC. I called her selfish and immature, but from the little I remember about book 1, she wasn't half the monster she became in book 2. Sorry, but there's no other way to put it. Mare is a monster. Forget Maven or Queen Elara. The real villain is your damn MC. I'm not going to go on about the lack of plot in "Glass Sword". For details on how the story was boring and led to nowhere surprising at all, you can find other reviews on Goodreads. Same for how the rest of the cast was uninteresting and one dimensional, or how the romance lacked chemistry. This review is solely focused on Mare and how she had me make over 50 notes on my Kindle it'd never happened before just because I couldn't stand reading about her and not marking all the places she was insufferable. One might be asking at this point why I kept reading if I hated it so much. Well, the train wreck theory explains it well. Google it. So, I'm going to write some of my Kindle notes so you get to experience what I did when reading about this selfish, despising character's thoughts. 1 Mare being her lovely self. Mare "now I know I am special" Me how many times is she going to call herself special in chapter one???? look at the question marks and you'll understand I'm already agitated, and it's 8 in Mare "I'm worth more than the rest". Me raises eyebrow Really? Did she... Did she just say that? Mare "I'm more valuable than most, because of what I've done and what I can do." Me here we go again. And why is she so valuable? There are so many others with more interesting abilities than her stupid lightining! 2 Mare being lovely to all her "friends" and "family" yes, quotation marks needed here Exhibit A Mare talking about Kilorn - the boy who's clearly stupid enough to stand by her side since childhood, always defend her and still find it in his heart to love her. I don't know what's wrong with him, but Kilorn has a serious problem. Mare "To think he's spending his time flirting while I've been unconscious..." Me Really? You want to control him even when you're unconscious? Great. Mare "Like a dog following commands." Me gasps Did she just say that about Kilorn? Great way to refer to a friend. rolls eyes Mare "He can weave a net faster than anyone I know, but what good is that when we're catching people, not fish? ... He survived the Hall of the Sun because of me, and outlived the massacre of Caesar's Square because of luck." Me She's so annoying. How is Kilorn still her friend? Someone explain that, please. Mare "Glad? You're jealous, plain and simple. You're not used to sharing. And you don't like being useless." Me Someone hold me back. Did she just say that? Did she just called him useless to his face? Then Kilorn stops talking to her and what does she do? Mare "If I were not so preoccupied with my own duties, recruiting and training, I would try and snap him out of it. But I barely have time to sleep, let alone coax Kilorn back into the fold." Me I didn't expect you to stop being selfish now. We're already 59 in. Mare "Who is he to question my orders? He's no one. A fish boy with only good luck and my foolishness to protect him." this right after her brother died Me WHAT??????????????????? I'm done. Exhibit B Mare when thinking or interacting with Shade, the brother who saved her more times than anyone can keep track. Mare "His face falls, torn by the knowledge that I will not save him." Me SELFISH!!! How can you leave your brother behind like this???? He'd never leave you!! And of course Shade had to die. No surprise there. Just as predictable as Maven being the bad guy in book 1. The only surprising aspect of it was when it would take place. Hmmm.. Not really. Shade would only be killed when he was not useful anymore, meaning when the author didn't need him to save Mare from the impossible situations she managed to get herself into. So she had to wait until the end of the book to do that, right? Yeah. No surprise. So, after Shade dies, what does the lovely MC do? Cry? Break down? Has a redeeming moment? Of course not. She verbally and physically abuses her brother's girlfriend, the only person mourning poor Shade. When the girlfriend tries to fight back, Mare acts like her lovely self again Mare "Farley, you never know when to quit. I used to admire you for it. Now I lonely pity you." Me Don't know why I'm surprised, but still can't believe she just said that. Exhibit C Mare being mean to her best friend and older brother isn't enough, so she needs to bully the rest of her family, too. Mare about her other brother "It's probably the smartest thing I've ever heard Bree say." Me OMG. I can't even. No words. Mare about her decision to NOT stop her siblings from going with her to a mission that will mostly end in their deaths five minutes after delivering the body of her dead older brother to her family "I wish I could tell them not to come. They would listen if I truly meant it. But I can't. I need them, just like I needed Shade." Me Yeah, and look at where that got him. Dead. Not enough to kill one brother, huh? 3 Mare caring about the only person she shouldn't. Here obsession with the one who betrayed and tried to kill her is still shocking to me. 13 in and I couldn't stand how many times she'd already thought about how much she missed Maven. He tried to kill you!!! Are you stupid or...? groans Then Maven starts leaving letters next to dead bodies of children and babies and PEOPLE saying he'll kill everyone if she doesn't go back to him. What does Mare think? "I miss him". 4 Mare being overdramatic. What about her non-stop overreaction to absolutely everything? Every-damn-thing pained her. Everything was more than she could bare. More than she could take, but she was soooo strong, so damn strong because she was the lightning girl and had to keep going so she could save the world. rolls eyes Please, have mercy! 5 Finally, the good parts. You know the little parts that didn't suck? They were the ones when other characters finally called her out on her bullshit. I lived for the moments those with a little bit more sense than the ones blindly following an incompetent leader Mare, in case you don't know who I'm talking about addressed the MC the way she deserved. Colonel "Not everything revolves around you, Miss Barrow. The world does not rise and fall at your command." Me YESSSS!!! If only the author understood this, too. Cameron my favorite character who obviously came into play way too late and disappeared shortly after with no reasonable explanation "'Don't act so high-and-mighty', she presses on, throwing words like daggers ... 'You're no lordy lady now, no matter how many of us you try to order around. Bedding a priencleing doesn't make you queen of the heap." Of course Mare goes on to call Cameron a bitch and a brat she needs to "educate" - this word was used. Educate. Really. I couldn't even make this stuff up. 6 The rest. Don't even get me started on the "amazing cliffhanger" everyone was going on about. Really? That was it? Really? After everything you read here, do you honestly think I care what happened to Mare????

Annith started out as a strong, intelligent, and independent woman, who takes her fate into her own hands when others try to force her into life choices she doesn't want. Normally, that would be right up my alley story-wise. But once Annith actually got out into the world, it felt like all she did was mourn about how wronged she felt by everyone she cam into contact with. The story very quickly deteriorated for me into a whine-fest, with relatively minimal actual story development. It felt like nothing had happened yet when I was almost a third through the story, and at that point I realized I was bored, so I gave up. This was just too much emotional drama without a plotline payoff for me.

There is nothing spectacular here and I find the writing too juvenile, which, I conclude isn't really a bad thing because it's obviously marketed towards the younger audience. I cannot really call it a "fail" book because I must admit I did enjoy reading this in a sort of this-is-silly-but-it's-cute-so-f ck-it kind of way. I like the main protagonist, Elise, because she's a witty narrator though very self-righteous at times. I also like Derek because he's cute. Don't expect to read complex characters here and thought provoking scenes. This book is just pure, mindless fun. My only complaint is that the ending felt rushed and it ended when the lovers are just starting to hit it off. I was kinda sad because I am a happily ever after kind of girl. It would be more awesome if there's an epilogue that says Elise and Derek got married 10 years later and had 3 kids and a dog, probably a German shepherd. You know, something like that? But over-all, it is a nice book. If you want a nice break from all the heavy drama books and wants a short and fun read with PG 13 romance then I recommend this book.

This book disappointed me so much, I'm just so happy it's over. Let me just say that this book was a mess. The only thing I really liked about it was that it was set in Canada and incorporated diversity. That's literally all I liked. I tried so hard to like this book, I really wanted to. The concept was so cool and unique, it held so much potential but fell so so flat. There is such poor writing in this book. I didn't like it at all. It dragged so much for the majority of the book, and I didn't think there was a very good explanation for anything, I was confused 90 of the time. I also found the development of the characters to be so very bad. They were all just so dull and I didn't find myself attaching or liking any of them. Especially Greta. She was so naive throughout this book, and if I may be honest, completely annoying. Her narration is so childish I would roll my eyes every other line. I have to use a direct quote here because I found it utterly ridiculous "The soldier was leading the horse with a... leading thing." That is just careless description and I've been seeing it more and more in YA and it bothers me so much. The writing wasn't as clear as it is in many other books I've read, I couldn't picture anything from this world in my mind. I've found that some unnecessary descriptions were way too detailed, but many more important descriptions weren't detailed enough. Another thing about Greta she was always trying to be the best, most bravest queen in all the land. She had to be strong because she was a queen. A queen must always keep her cool. So when her friends are in a gun fight, instead of coming to their aid, Greta decides to SIT DOWN. She tried so hard to be noble, she always thought she was doing the noble thing. Sorry, no. Never in my life have I read about such a weak character. Gosh. Talis was made to be the funny, spunky, likable villain. But it was too forced and didn't feel real. I also didn't like the pedestal Greta put Xie on for the whole book. Any time she'd look at her she'd call her a goddess. The description of Xie constantly included 'goddess' in there somewhere. "She is a goddess-queen in red and gold silk..." I'm not going to spoil anything but the even that happened at the end bothered me so much. I didn't like where it went and frankly, it just added to my confusion. Nothing was explained clearly to me this is just how I felt about the clarity of the writing, I may just be incredibly oblivious at this point in the novel because I'm skimming pages to get it over with . I was seriously considering DNFing this book but I didn't because I wanted to share my thoughts. I'm so disappointed, I was so excited about this book because it's a great concept. It was just so poorly executed. Overall, I didn't like this book at all. This was the worst book I've read in a while. But I have heard other people say they enjoyed this book so it depends on the person. I won't be continuing on with the series and I don't think I'll be reading any more of Bow's books. This was so painful to read.

Charlie is the not only the dork of his senior high school class, is singled out for harassment for being gay, and is a huge disappointment to his father. Not only that, but his best friend since second grade now has a girlfriend, so he finds himself with a lot of time on his hands and a lot of time with his hands on his dick . When cute and popular new student Rob shows an interest in him, Charlie keeps thinking it must be a mistake, but he soon finds himself with a boyfriend and even more reason to focus on his dick . Both Rob and Charlie have parent problems Rob's parents are loving and supportive, but his mom is dying of Lou Gehrig's disease, and Charlie's parents seem headed for a divorce. When Rob's mom dies things blow up for everyone as Rob's father is accused of assisted suicide. A little too much detailed jerking-off action for me, but a realistic portrayal of of horny teenage boyhood, and the fact that it was well-written kept me reading. Obviously a good choice for gay teens.

I won a hardcover copy of this in a giveaway, so thanks so much to Christina at The Paperback Princesses and Simon Schuster! Instead of breaking it down to what I liked what I didn't like, I wrote down some thoughts about it some mild spoilers ahead -What the heck is the timeline for these events? When did Arthur his dad die? How long has it been since Anne's mom remarried? How long were Henry Anne together? So many questions. -When will YA books realize that a "different" piercing i.e. not your ears does not make you "bad"? I mean, yeah, Henry thought it was hot, but I think he said that in the same breath as "she looks like trouble" or something along those lines. -There was a lot of emotion in the book but it seemed like it was just thrown in there without buildup one minute Henry was worried. Then he was angry. Then he was drooling all over Anne. All in the span of two minutes. -At the same time, most of their emotions felt superficial. If I had to read "s he is hot" one more time, I was going to lose my head mind. -Henry was such a dick. I'm sure Henry VIII was also a dick, but at least he was a king and you could understand why all the ladies were okay with being used by him. This Henry, though, is the school president, and too much of a tool to be attractive sorry . I don't know why Anne or Catherine, for that matter , put up with him. -I kinda liked the spin on Mary Boleyn, but it could have been really interesting if Henry had known her before like in One Tree Hill when Nathan realizes how he knows Hayley's sister Taylor wink wink . -Key historical figures not included that could have made the book more scandalous Mary and Elizabeth Tudor. Also George Boleyn. -Anne was the most developed character but then she went from "badass who doesn't care" to "falling all over herself for her toolbox of a boyfriend" when she could have been powerful. Everyone else felt two dimensional and disingenuous like they were being forced to talk act a certain way , plus some of them disappeared halfway through before being brought back for the culminating scene Sam and Charles, I'm talking about you . -The horse on the beach. I just...I don't know what to say. -I did like the way they dealt with Anne's "beheading" and the introduction of Jane Seymour. -Stylistically, there were some sentences that were broken up like this and I found it annoying. But that's just me! Maybe other people think it's fun or creates a certain emphasis or tone? I don't know. At the end of the day, when you take away the historical context, it's nothing but a petty high school drama with a massive dose of insta-love. The stakes aren't as high for teen-Henry as they were for his kingly counterpart did teen-Henry have to leave the church and form his own church just to get out of a relationship? No, he just had to make up his mind . Nevertheless, there's something compulsively readable about Anne Henry. I didn't particularly care for any of the characters, but I still wanted to find out what happened next. I imagine it will appeal to fans of Gossip Girl and the like I've never read a Gossip Girl book, but I've watched the whole show . If it hadn't been for the historical ties, it's not something I would normally be into. And the more I think about it, the more annoyed I feel.

My friend gave me this book to read, which was great, since I already had in mind to read it. Rainbow Boys was a really good and wonderful coming out story. This worked really nicely, since Jason, Nelson and Kyle were their own personas with an actual voice of their own. I'm happy that Sanchez had the talent to give life to his characters and make me believe in them. The plot works and it was great how important issues were addressed, such as HIV and bullying, without making the book too educational. This is a really fine book for people still in the closet or actually, to everyone gay or straight. I'm just a bit sad how the book didn't have an ending of its own, but was left too open for the sequel. It also bothered me somewhat how Nelson was always lighting his cigarettes or throwing up, since he seemed to gather too many problems for one person. Perhaps the possible HIV case would've sufficed. Otherwise I'd say that this story was a steady and wonderful case to be read in schools everywhere I'd even say.

Dash Lily's Book of Dares is a YA contemporary novel set at Christmas in New York, and because it's set during the festive period, that was when I had intended to read it. However, things don't always work out the way you plan them, and so I ended up reading this in March but it was snowing, so I guess the weather was good for it! . I'm telling you this because I want to make it clear that although this is a fairly festive novel, it isn't exclusively so, and I enjoyed it just as much now as I think I would have done reading it at Christmas. In fact, reading it later in the year is nice - it extends the Christmas cheer into the rest of the year! My initial impression of this book was very good. The chapters alternate between Dash and Lily, the two protagonists, and the opening chapter introduces us to Dash. Straight away I had a clear sense of his character I knew that he was adventurous and inquisitive he found the red notebook, and immediately opened it and starting following the dares inside , and that he doesn't like Christmas 'It was Christmastime in New York City, the most detestable time of the year' . This is a good start, but it's not all there is to his character. As we see more of him and his chapters, I learnt more about his character, and although I wasn't particularly endeared to him at first mostly due to his Christmas-hating tendencies, in all honesty , I gradually started to fall for his character. He's witty, sarcastic and loyal, and I really enjoyed getting to see his character change as he and Lily interacted more and more through the notebook. The alternate chapters to Dash's then, are Lily's. Lily seems to be, at first, Dash's total opposite. Whereas one of the first things we learn about him is that he hates Christmas, the very first thing we learn about Lily is that she loves it - in fact, it's almost as though she lives and breaths it. We soon learn that she's an avid caroller, so much so that she organisers her own carolling society, and that ever since she was little, she's kept a journal in red moleskin notebooks - the very same that Dash finds in the bookstore in the first chapter. Lily is a very sweet and positive character, and I liked her almost instantly - I think it's just all her Christmas cheer that was rubbing off on me! She was very funny - perhaps not in a witty way, like Dash is although she is some of the time - but she made me laugh all the same. At the beginning of the book, although she was confident in some areas like her carolling , she definitely needed a confidence boost in others like meeting boys , and see Langston, her brother, gives her that push and convinces her to write a series of dares in one of her red moleskins, and to leave it in the bookstore for a boy to pick up. Her Christmas this year is different - her parents are away in Fiji, and her brother is busy with his new boyfriend, Benny, so Lily is left to celebrate the Christmas period on her own - that is, until Dash takes her up on her dares, and they start their pen and paper conversation that takes them all over New York. I loved their interaction through the notebook, and just like both of them, I was eagerly anticipating what was going to be written in the notebook next, where they would find it, and the kind of dares that they would both have to do. It was a really interesting and unique way for the two characters to interact, and I enjoyed every twist and turn in their written journey. But what I really wanted to see was the two of them meeting for the first time - in person. Obviously this was not destined to go smoothly - there wouldn't be much to the story if they met and lived happily ever after - but part of me still hoped! Despite little hiccups along the way though, I really loved the way that Dash Lily's story came to an end at least the story that we see in the novel - I have a feeling their story will go on far beyond the pages! . Dash Lily's story was exactly the kind I needed at the moment it was light-hearted, funny, witty, intelligent but still an easy read , optimistic and festive. It was exactly the kind of pick-me-up I needed, and I really enjoyed it. It wasn't quite what I expected from the story - which I can't really explain - but I enjoyed it all the same. I loved Dash Lily's characters, and I also enjoyed the characters that surrounded them, especially Boomer Dash's best friend , Langston Lily's brother and Mrs. Basil E. Lily's nicknamed great aunt . The story was really cute, and it kept me gripped all the way through. I definitely recommend this one to any fan of YA contemporary or contemporary in general, because I think it's such a clever and witty book that readers of any age would enjoy it , whether it's Christmastime or not! A seriously enjoyable read.

Are webcomics still a thing? I know they were a pretty big thing about ten years ago when I was still in high school. I kept tabs on about a dozen of them, half of which updated regularly, none of which I can remember ever finishing. As someone who wrote and drew regularly, I constantly considered starting my own webcomic. I rarely made it past the first two pages. It turns out that writing and illustrating comics is really hard, and more than talent, it requires dedication to a single idea for years, often with little to no notice or appreciation from others. Francesca Zappia has definitely read webcomics. She gets it. That was my prevailing thought while reading 'Eliza and Her Monsters'- that Zappia gets it. The fandom, the unfinished masterpieces, the legitimacy of fanworks, even her fictional webcomic idea is exactly the sort of thing I could see topping the top rated lists. Zappia knows her stuff and as a result, reading her book was like talking to a fandom friend thoroughly enjoyable and eminently relatable. I think anyone who's ever enjoyed webcomics or online fandom will get a kick out of this book.

Fury is a very hard book for me to rate. While on one hand I can see that it is a very well written book, on the other hand I didn't enjoy it at all. So I'm really not sure what to rate the book as. I feel that it isn't fair to rate this a 1 star because honestly, it's a very very very well written book. On the other hand I didn't enjoy this at all so hmmm choices choices! I think the author Shirley Marr is an excellent writer. She takes what is essentially a simple storyline but through witty sharp writing and excellent plotting manages to turn it into something complex and thought provoking. The book starts of with main character Eliza Boans getting interrogated in a holding room over a murder she committed. The book then brilliant weaves the present and the past as the authorities try to uncover what really happened and the most important question of them all why did it happen? Very reminiscent of movies like "The Machinist" and "Memento Mori". As a reader, you start of the story as clueless as the Doctor who is interrogating Eliza and just like him, you can't wait to figure out the mystery behind the murder. Just like "The Machinist" and "Memento Mori", although Fury reveals the mystery of the murder, the ending is ambiguous and lets the reader interpret what will happen next even after the book closes. For me this type of story format works better with an open ended ending - one that the reader can imagine for himself herself. However, her characters is what really killed the book for me though. Fury initially appears to be a Mean Girls copycat on the surface with the main character Eliza Boans quite the dead ringer for our dear Regina Rachel McAdams but like an iceberg floating in the sea, there's more to these girls that's hidden beneath the surface. Like Regina, she's spoiled, rich, arrogant, bratty and is the Queen Bee of her own little girl group that compromises of Lexi, Marianne and newcomer Ella all who are also under arrest . They start off as caricatures of a Queen Bee group but towards the end of the book turn into actual complicated and very real girls. They have fierce rivalries with strange loyalties yet there's backstabbing and plotting amongst each other, yeah they totally take the word "Freenemy" to a whole different level. These girls represent everything I hate about 'bitchy friendships' and it was quite difficult reading though Eliza's narration without feeling contempt for her and her friends. Having said that, I think essentially this is THEIR story. I don't think the author had any intentions for the readers to like her characters. It's as if this is some kind of Nat Geo documentary on Queen Bee High school relationships. If the characters were any different, I don't think the story would have worked which is why despite my contempt for all of them, I am able to objectively see the story for what it is - a well written story about bitchy high school relationships with a murder thrown in. Now if you don't really care for reading about a bunch of mean girls backstabbing each other and the complexities of their friendship, then Fury is definitely not for you which sadly is what I felt about the book. But if you're looking for a well written book about the complexities of bitchy female friendships, then don't give Fury a skip! PS I think the material would have been quite an awesome Indie Movie, think Girl Interrupted along the likes. PPS Despite not liking Fury, I have become quite the fan of Shirley Marr and would def pick up any new books from her well depending on subject material of course, if it's abt bitch high school girls again maybe not . That just shows what a brilliant writer she is.

From there we see her try and find distractions from playing sports to putting her all in getting good grades to not doing anything. We see her go from trying to figure out what college she wants to go to, to being a sixth grader and having fun with her two best friends. In between these two times we also get to see her like a boy, get the pets she's always wanted, go to trial to try and convict the man who stole her best friend. Overall I thought this story was okay. The format of going back from tenth grade all the way to sixth was a little confusing at times, but it showed more of what happened and what the main character had been like before.
